+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/start_review.sh against a local stub of the cloud routine.
+# Usage: tests/start_review_test.sh [path/to/start_review.sh]
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+script=${1:-$repo/scripts/start_review.sh}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat >"$work/stub.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, pathlib, sys
+work = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        (work / "request.json").write_text(json.dumps({
+            "path": self.path,
+            "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+            "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+            "body": json.loads(body),
+        }))
+        status = int((work / "status").read_text())
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"routine says hello")
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+(work / "port").write_text(str(server.server_port))
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 -I "$work/stub.py" "$work" &
+server_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+port=$(cat "$work/port")
+
+failures=0
+check() { # name expected_exit status
+  echo "$3" >"$work/status"
+  rm -f "$work/request.json"
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/fire" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret-token \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=model-x REVIEW_EFFORT=high PATH="$work/nobin:$PATH" \
+    bash "$script" 42 >"$work/out" 2>&1
+  actual=$?
+  if [ "$actual" != "$2" ]; then
+    echo "FAIL $1: exit $actual, want $2"; cat "$work/out"; failures=$((failures + 1)); return
+  fi
+  if ! jq -e '.path == "/fire"
+      and .authorization == "Bearer secret-token"
+      and (.content_type | startswith("application/json"))
+      and .body == {"pull_request": 42, "model": "model-x", "effort": "high"}' \
+      "$work/request.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "FAIL $1: wrong request"; cat "$work/request.json" 2>/dev/null; failures=$((failures + 1)); return
+  fi
+  if grep -q secret-token "$work/out"; then
+    echo "FAIL $1: token printed"; failures=$((failures + 1)); return
+  fi
+  echo "ok   $1"
+}
+
+check "200 passes" 0 200
+check "422 fails" 1 422
+check "500 fails" 1 500
+
+[ "$failures" = 0 ] && echo "all passed" || { echo "$failures failed"; exit 1; }

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs start_review.sh against a mock cloud routine and checks the exit code
+# and request for each routine response status.
+set -euo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -r -- "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/mock.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, os, sys
+status_file, log_file = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(log_file, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"path": self.path, "type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"), "auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(open(status_file).read()))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
+EOF
+port=18765
+python3 -I "$work/mock.py" "$port" "$work/status" "$work/request.json" &
+server_pid=$!
+sleep 1
+
+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/fire"
+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token
+export REVIEW_MODEL='model "x"'
+export REVIEW_EFFORT=high
+
+failures=0
+check() {
+  local status=$1 want=$2 got=0
+  echo "$status" > "$work/status"
+  rm -f -- "$work/request.json"
+  bash "$here/start_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1 || got=$?
+  if [ "$want" = 0 ] && [ "$got" != 0 ]; then echo "FAIL: $status gave exit $got, want 0"; failures=$((failures+1)); return; fi
+  if [ "$want" != 0 ] && [ "$got" = 0 ]; then echo "FAIL: $status gave exit 0, want non-zero"; failures=$((failures+1)); return; fi
+  if [ ! -f "$work/request.json" ]; then echo "FAIL: $status sent no request"; failures=$((failures+1)); return; fi
+  if ! jq -e '.path == "/fire" and .type == "application/json" and .auth == "Bearer test-token" and .body == {"pull_request": 42, "model": "model \"x\"", "effort": "high"}' "$work/request.json" >/dev/null; then
+    echo "FAIL: $status sent wrong request: $(cat "$work/request.json")"; failures=$((failures+1)); return
+  fi
+  echo "ok: $status -> exit $got"
+}
+check 200 0
+check 422 1
+check 500 1
+check 401 1
+[ "$failures" = 0 ] && echo PASS || { echo "FAILED: $failures"; exit 1; }

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review runs through the cloud routine and never on the desktop runner.
+# Usage: tests/test_cloud_review.sh
+#   ROOT=<dir>    tree to check (default: the repository)
+#   SCRIPT=<file> cloud review script to exercise (default: $ROOT/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh)
+set -uo pipefail
+ROOT=${ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)}
+SCRIPT=${SCRIPT:-$ROOT/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh}
+failures=0
+pass() { echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { echo "FAIL $1"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+check() { if eval "$2"; then pass "$1"; else fail "$1"; fi; }
+
+pr=$ROOT/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml
+rr=$ROOT/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml
+
+# Static checks on the workflows.
+check "no workflow uses the desktop runner" "! grep -rq desktop '$ROOT/.github/workflows'"
+check "start_review.sh is gone" "[ ! -e '$ROOT/scripts/start_review.sh' ]"
+check "no workflow calls start_review.sh" "! grep -rq 'start_review\.sh' '$ROOT/.github/workflows'"
+for wf in "$pr" "$rr"; do
+  name=$(basename "$wf")
+  check "$name runs on ubuntu-latest" "[ \"\$(yq -r '.jobs.review.\"runs-on\"' '$wf')\" = ubuntu-latest ]"
+  check "$name calls start_cloud_review.sh" "grep -q 'scripts/start_cloud_review.sh' '$wf'"
+  check "$name opens, reviews, completes in order" "[ \"\$(yq -c '[.jobs.review.steps[].name | select(. != null)]' '$wf')\" = '[\"Open check run\",\"Start cloud review\",\"Complete check run\"]' ]"
+  check "$name review step gets the routine URL from vars" "[ \"\$(yq -r '.jobs.review.steps[] | select(.name == \"Start cloud review\") | .env.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL' '$wf')\" = '\${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}' ]"
+  check "$name review step gets the token from secrets" "[ \"\$(yq -r '.jobs.review.steps[] | select(.name == \"Start cloud review\") | .env.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN' '$wf')\" = '\${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}' ]"
+  check "$name completes ai-review always" "[ \"\$(yq -r '.jobs.review.steps[] | select(.name == \"Complete check run\") | .if' '$wf')\" = 'always()' ]"
+done
+check "pr-review triggers unchanged" "[ \"\$(yq -c '.on' '$pr')\" = '{\"pull_request\":{\"types\":[\"opened\",\"synchronize\"]}}' ]"
+check "rerun-review triggers unchanged" "[ \"\$(yq -c '.on' '$rr')\" = '{\"issue_comment\":{\"types\":[\"created\"]}}' ]"
+check "rerun-review filter unchanged" "[ \"\$(yq -r '.jobs.review.if' '$rr')\" = \"github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')\" ]"
+for s in check_run.sh start_cloud_review.sh; do
+  check "$s is executable in git" "git -C '$ROOT' ls-files -s 'scripts/$s' | grep -q '^100755 '"
+done
+check "curl stops before 31 minutes" "grep -q -- '--max-time 1860' '$SCRIPT'"
+
+# Behaviour checks of the script against a local fake routine.
+if [ ! -x "$SCRIPT" ]; then
+  fail "cloud review script exists and is executable"
+else
+  work=$(mktemp -d)
+  python3 -I - "$work" <<'PY' &
+import http.server, sys, os
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "request"), "w") as f:
+            f.write(self.headers.get("Authorization", "") + "\n" + body.decode())
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+with open(os.path.join(work, "port.tmp"), "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(s.server_port))
+os.rename(os.path.join(work, "port.tmp"), os.path.join(work, "port"))
+s.serve_forever()
+PY
+  server=$!
+  trap 'kill $server 2>/dev/null; find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -f "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done

+  run() {
+    REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok123 \
+      CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="$1" "$SCRIPT" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  }
+  check "HTTP 200 passes" "run http://127.0.0.1:$port/200"
+  check "request carries the bearer token" "[ \"\$(head -1 '$work/request')\" = 'Bearer tok123' ]"
+  check "request body is pull_request, model, effort" "[ \"\$(tail -n +2 '$work/request' | jq -cS .)\" = '{\"effort\":\"high\",\"model\":\"m1\",\"pull_request\":42}' ]"

+  check "HTTP 500 fails" "! run http://127.0.0.1:$port/500"
+  check "HTTP 202 fails" "! run http://127.0.0.1:$port/202"
+  check "unreachable routine fails" "! run http://127.0.0.1:1/200"
+  check "missing token fails" "! env -u CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$port/200 '$SCRIPT' 42 >/dev/null 2>&1"
+fi
+
+echo "$failures failure(s)"

+# Exits 0 only when the routine returns 200. There is no local fallback.
 set -euo pipefail
 pull_request_number=$1
-reviewer exec review \
-  --model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
-  --effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
-  --pull-request "$pull_request_number" \
-  --post-comments
+: "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}"
+if [[ ! $pull_request_number =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+  echo "pull request number must be numeric: $pull_request_number" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
+for value in "$REVIEW_MODEL" "$REVIEW_EFFORT"; do
+  if [[ ! $value =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$ ]]; then
+    echo "model and effort may hold only letters, digits and . _ : -: $value" >&2
+    exit 2
+  fi
+done
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%s,"model":"%s","effort":"%s"}' \
+  "$pull_request_number" "$REVIEW_MODEL" "$REVIEW_EFFORT")
+response=$(mktemp)
+trap 'rm -f "$response"' EXIT
+rc=0
+# The header goes in on stdin so the token does not show in the process list.
+status=$(printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" |
+  curl --silent --show-error --config - \
+    --max-time 1860 \
+    --request POST \
+    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    --data "$body" \
+    --output "$response" \
+    --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+    "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL") || rc=$?
+cat "$response"
+if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
+  echo "cloud routine call failed: curl exit $rc" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "cloud review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "cloud review reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "cloud routine failed: HTTP $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review goes through the cloud routine with no desktop runner.
+# Run from anywhere: tests/review_cloud_test.sh
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+workflows=("$root/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml" "$root/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml")
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+pass() { echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { echo "FAIL $1"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+check() { if eval "$2"; then pass "$1"; else fail "$1"; fi; }
+
+# Workflow checks.
+for wf in "${workflows[@]}"; do
+  name=$(basename "$wf")
+  check "$name has no desktop runner" "! grep -q 'desktop' '$wf'"
+  check "$name runs on the NAS" "grep -q 'runs-on: \[self-hosted, nas\]' '$wf'"
+  check "$name has no concurrency group" "! grep -q '^ *concurrency:' '$wf'"
+  check "$name has timeout-minutes >= 32" \
+    "[[ \$(grep -oP 'timeout-minutes: \K[0-9]+' '$wf') -ge 32 ]]"
+  check "$name keeps opening the check run" "grep -q 'scripts/check_run.sh open' '$wf'"
+  check "$name keeps completing the check run with if: always()" \
+    "grep -B1 'scripts/check_run.sh complete' '$wf' | grep -q 'if: always()'"
+  check "$name calls scripts/start_review.sh" "grep -q 'scripts/start_review.sh' '$wf'"
+  check "$name passes the cloud routine URL and token" \
+    "grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: \${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}' '$wf' && grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: \${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}' '$wf'"
+done
+pr="${workflows[0]}"
+rerun="${workflows[1]}"
+check "pr-review triggers on pull_request opened, synchronize" \
+  "grep -q '^  pull_request:' '$pr' && grep -q 'types: \[opened, synchronize\]' '$pr'"
+check "rerun-review triggers on issue_comment created with /rereview" \
+  "grep -q '^  issue_comment:' '$rerun' && grep -q 'types: \[created\]' '$rerun' && grep -q \"startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')\" '$rerun'"
+check "no script or workflow runs the reviewer CLI" \
+  "! grep -rqE '(^|[^-])reviewer exec' '$root/scripts' '$root/.github'"
+
+# Script checks with stub curl and a stub reviewer that records any call.
+mkdir -p "$work/bin"
+cat > "$work/bin/curl" <<'STUB'
+#!/bin/bash
+cat > "$STUB_DIR/stdin"
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_DIR/args"
+out=
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  [[ $1 == --output ]] && out=$2
+  shift
+done
+[[ -n $out ]] && echo '{"stub":true}' > "$out"
+if [[ ${STUB_RC:-0} -ne 0 ]]; then
+  echo "curl: stub error $STUB_RC" >&2
+  exit "$STUB_RC"
+fi
+printf '%s' "$STUB_STATUS"
+STUB
+cat > "$work/bin/reviewer" <<'STUB'
+#!/bin/bash
+touch "$STUB_DIR/reviewer-called"
+exit 0
+STUB
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl" "$work/bin/reviewer"
+
+run_script() {
+  # run_script <pr> <status> <curl rc> [model]
+  rm -f "$work/reviewer-called" "$work/args" "$work/stdin"
+  env PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" STUB_DIR="$work" STUB_STATUS="$2" STUB_RC="$3" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/run CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret-token \
+    REVIEW_MODEL="${4:-model-1}" REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" "$1" > "$work/out" 2>&1
+}
+
+run_script 42 200 0; rc=$?
+check "HTTP 200 exits 0" "[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]"
+check "the request goes to CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL" "grep -qx 'https://routine.example/run' '$work/args'"
+check "the request carries all three JSON fields" \
+  "grep -qxF '{\"pull_request\":42,\"model\":\"model-1\",\"effort\":\"high\"}' '$work/args'"
+check "the bearer token goes in on stdin" "grep -q 'Authorization: Bearer secret-token' '$work/stdin'"
+check "the token is not on the command line" "! grep -q 'secret-token' '$work/args'"
+check "curl waits at least 30 minutes" \
+  "[[ \$(grep -A1 -x -- '--max-time' '$work/args' | tail -1) -ge 1800 ]]"
+
+for case in "422 0" "500 0" "000 7" "000 28"; do
+  set -- $case
+  run_script 42 "$1" "$2"; rc=$?
+  check "HTTP $1 with curl exit $2 exits non-zero" "[[ $rc -ne 0 ]]"
+  check "HTTP $1 with curl exit $2 does not fall back to the reviewer CLI" "[[ ! -e '$work/reviewer-called' ]]"
+done
+
+run_script abc 200 0; rc=$?
+check "a non-numeric pull request number is rejected" "[[ $rc -ne 0 && ! -e '$work/args' ]]"
+run_script 42 200 0 'bad"model'; rc=$?
+check "a model with a quote is rejected" "[[ $rc -ne 0 && ! -e '$work/args' ]]"
+
+echo
+if [[ $failures -gt 0 ]]; then
+  echo "$failures check(s) failed"
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "all checks passed"

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+url=${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}
+token=${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}
+model=${REVIEW_MODEL:?}
+effort=${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}
+if [[ ! $pull_request_number =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+  echo "pull request number must be numeric: $pull_request_number" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
+json_string() {
+  local s=${1//\\/\\\\}
+  s=${s//\"/\\\"}
+  printf '"%s"' "$s"
+}
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%s,"model":%s,"effort":%s}' \
+  "$pull_request_number" "$(json_string "$model")" "$(json_string "$effort")")
+# The routine holds the request open for up to 30 minutes. The token goes
+# through curl's stdin config so it never appears in the process list.
+status=$(printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$token" | curl -sS -K - \
+  --max-time 1900 \
+  -X POST "$url" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data-raw "$body" \
+  -o /dev/null \
+  -w '%{http_code}') || {
+  echo "cloud routine request failed" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "cloud review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "cloud review reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "cloud routine failed with HTTP $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac

+"""Stand-in for the cloud routine: answers with a fixed status and records each request."""
+import glob
+import http.server
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+
+status, record_path = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
+token = os.environ["MOCK_TOKEN"]
+
+
+def token_in_argv():
+    for path in glob.glob("/proc/[0-9]*/cmdline"):
+        try:
+            with open(path, "rb") as f:
+                if token.encode() in f.read():
+                    return True
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+    return False
+
+
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(record_path, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({
+                "body": body.decode(),
+                "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                "token_in_argv": token_in_argv(),
+            }, f)
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+print(server.server_port, flush=True)
+server.handle_request()

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review runs through the cloud routine and never on the desktop runner.
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+script=$root/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+failures=0
+token="tok-$RANDOM$RANDOM$RANDOM"
+
+check() {
+  if eval "$2"; then echo "ok   $1"; else echo "FAIL $1"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+
+# Workflows
+for wf in "$root"/.github/workflows/*.yml; do
+  name=$(basename "$wf")
+  check "$name: no desktop runner" "! grep -q 'desktop' '$wf'"
+  check "$name: no local reviewer script" "! grep -q 'start_review.sh' '$wf'"
+  check "$name: runs on the nas runner" "grep -qx '    runs-on: \[self-hosted, nas\]' '$wf'"
+  check "$name: job timeout above the 31-minute curl limit" \
+    "t=\$(sed -n 's/^    timeout-minutes: \([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' '$wf'); [ -n \"\$t\" ] && [ \"\$t\" -gt 31 ]"
+  check "$name: calls the cloud routine" "grep -q 'scripts/start_cloud_review.sh' '$wf'"
+  check "$name: passes the routine URL and token" \
+    "grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: \${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}' '$wf' && grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: \${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}' '$wf'"
+  check "$name: always completes the check run with the job status" \
+    "grep -A1 'name: Complete check run' '$wf' | grep -q 'if: always()' && grep -q 'check_run.sh complete .*\${{ job.status }}' '$wf'"
+done
+pr=$root/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml
+rr=$root/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml
+check "pr-review: same trigger as before" \
+  "grep -A1 '^  pull_request:' '$pr' | grep -q 'types: \[opened, synchronize\]'"
+check "rerun-review: same trigger as before" \
+  "grep -A1 '^  issue_comment:' '$rr' | grep -q 'types: \[created\]' && grep -qF \"if: github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')\" '$rr'"
+check "rerun-review: open and complete use one resolved head commit" \
+  "[ \$(grep -c 'check_run.sh \(open\|complete\) \"\${{ steps.head.outputs.sha }}\"' '$rr') -eq 2 ]"
+
+for f in check_run.sh start_cloud_review.sh; do
+  check "$f is executable" "[ -x '$root/scripts/$f' ]"
+done
+
+# Script behavior against a mock routine
+run_case() { # status pr model effort -> sets rc and rec
+  local port
+  rec=$work/record.json
+  : > "$rec"
+  MOCK_TOKEN="$token" python3 "$root/tests/mock_routine.py" "$1" "$rec" > "$work/port" &
+  local pid=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+  port=$(cat "$work/port")
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN="$token" \
+    REVIEW_MODEL="$3" REVIEW_EFFORT="$4" "$script" "$2" > /dev/null 2>&1
+  rc=$?
+  wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
+}
+
+if [ ! -x "$script" ]; then
+  check "start_cloud_review.sh exists and is executable" "false"
+else
+  run_case 200 42 'm"x\y' high
+  check "200 passes" "[ $rc -eq 0 ]"
+  check "body carries pull_request, model and effort with escaping" \
+    "python3 -c 'import json,sys; b=json.loads(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))[\"body\"]); sys.exit(b!={\"pull_request\":42,\"model\":\"m\\\"x\\\\y\",\"effort\":\"high\"})' '$rec'"
+  check "bearer token sent" "grep -q \"\\\"authorization\\\": \\\"Bearer $token\\\"\" '$rec'"
+  check "token not in any process argv" "grep -q '\"token_in_argv\": false' '$rec'"
+  run_case 422 42 m high
+  check "422 fails" "[ $rc -eq 1 ]"
+  run_case 500 42 m high
+  check "500 fails" "[ $rc -eq 1 ]"
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:9/" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e \
+    "$script" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+  check "unreachable routine fails" "[ $? -ne 0 ]"
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:9/" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e \
+    "$script" '1,"x":2' > /dev/null 2>&1
+  check "non-numeric pull request rejected" "[ $? -ne 0 ]"
+  env -u CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:9/" REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e \
+    "$script" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+  check "missing token fails" "[ $? -ne 0 ]"
+fi
+
+echo "failures: $failures"
+[ "$failures" -eq 0 ]

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review goes through the cloud routine and never the desktop.
+# Usage: tests/test_cloud_review.sh  (needs bash, curl, python3)
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+server_pid=
+cleanup() {
+  [[ -n $server_pid ]] && kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null
+  find "$work" -mindepth 1 -delete && rmdir "$work"
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+failures=0
+check() {
+  if eval "$2"; then echo "ok   $1"; else echo "FAIL $1"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+
+# A reviewer stub on PATH that exits 0, so a hidden desktop fallback would turn a failure into a pass.
+mkdir "$work/bin"
+printf '#!/bin/bash\necho called >> %q\n' "$work/reviewer_calls" > "$work/bin/reviewer"
+chmod +x "$work/bin/reviewer"
+
+# Mock routine: answers with the status in $work/status and records the request.
+cat > "$work/mock.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, pathlib, sys
+work = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))).decode()
+        (work / "request.json").write_text(json.dumps({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": body}))
+        self.send_response(int((work / "status").read_text()))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+(work / "port").write_text(str(server.server_port))
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 "$work/mock.py" "$work" &
+server_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [[ -s $work/port ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+url="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/review"
+
+run_review() {
+  env PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="$1" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN="${4:-secret-token}" \
+    REVIEW_MODEL="${3:-model-a}" REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" "$2" > "$work/out" 2>&1
+}
+
+echo 200 > "$work/status"
+run_review "$url" 42; code=$?
+check "200 exits 0" '[[ $code -eq 0 ]]'
+check "sends bearer token" 'python3 -c "import json,sys; assert json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))[\"auth\"] == \"Bearer secret-token\"" "$work/request.json"'
+check "sends pull_request, model, effort" 'python3 -c "import json,sys; b = json.loads(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))[\"body\"]); assert b == {\"pull_request\": 42, \"model\": \"model-a\", \"effort\": \"high\"}, b" "$work/request.json"'
+
+: > "$work/request.json"
+run_review "$url" 42 'org/model[1m]' 'to"k\en'; code=$?
+check "model with / and [ ] is accepted" '[[ $code -eq 0 ]]'
+check "token with quote and backslash is sent intact" 'python3 -c "import json,sys; assert json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))[\"auth\"] == sys.argv[2]" "$work/request.json" "Bearer to\"k\\en"'
+
+echo 422 > "$work/status"
+run_review "$url" 42; code=$?
+check "422 exits non-zero" '[[ $code -ne 0 ]]'
+check "422 reports blocking findings" 'grep -q "blocking findings" "$work/out"'
+
+echo 500 > "$work/status"
+run_review "$url" 42; code=$?
+check "500 exits non-zero" '[[ $code -ne 0 ]]'
+check "500 reports routine failure" 'grep -q "status 500" "$work/out"'
+
+run_review "http://127.0.0.1:1/review" 42; code=$?
+check "unreachable routine exits non-zero" '[[ $code -ne 0 ]] && grep -q "status 000" "$work/out"'
+
+request_file="$work/request.json"; : > "$request_file"
+run_review "$url" "42; x" ; code=$?
+check "invalid pull request number is rejected" '[[ $code -ne 0 && ! -s $request_file ]]'
+run_review "$url" 42 'bad"model'; code=$?
+check "invalid model is rejected" '[[ $code -ne 0 && ! -s $request_file ]]'
+run_review "$url" 42 model-a $'abc\nverbose'; code=$?
+check "token with a line break is rejected" '[[ $code -ne 0 && ! -s $request_file ]]'
+
+check "reviewer CLI is never called" '[[ ! -e $work/reviewer_calls ]]'
+
+for wf in "$repo"/.github/workflows/*.yml; do
+  name=$(basename "$wf")
+  check "$name has no desktop runner" '! grep -q desktop "$wf"'
+  if grep -q start_review.sh "$wf"; then
+    check "$name runs on the NAS" 'grep -q "runs-on: \[self-hosted, nas\]" "$wf"'
+    check "$name sets timeout-minutes" 'grep -q "timeout-minutes:" "$wf"'
+    check "$name passes CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL" 'grep -q "CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: \${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}" "$wf"'
+    check "$name passes CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" 'grep -q "CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: \${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}" "$wf"'
+    check "$name still opens the check run" 'grep -q "scripts/check_run.sh open" "$wf"'
+    check "$name always completes the check run with job.status" 'grep -A1 "if: always()" "$wf" | grep -q "scripts/check_run.sh complete.*job.status"'
+  fi
+done
+check "pr-review.yml triggers on pull_request opened and synchronize" 'grep -A1 "^  pull_request:" "$repo/.github/workflows/pr-review.yml" | grep -q "types: \[opened, synchronize\]"'
+check "rerun-review.yml triggers on a /rereview comment" 'grep -A1 "^  issue_comment:" "$repo/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml" | grep -q "types: \[created\]" && grep -q "if: github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '"'"'/rereview'"'"')" "$repo/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml"'
+
+echo "$failures failure(s)"
+[[ $failures -eq 0 ]]

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that every review runs through the cloud routine with no desktop runner.
+set -uo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+failures=0
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+pass() { echo "ok:   $*"; }
+
+# 1. Every job runs on a GitHub-hosted runner, with a job timeout.
+for wf in .github/workflows/pr-review.yml .github/workflows/rerun-review.yml; do
+  runs_on=$(grep -E '^\s+runs-on:' "$wf" | sed -E 's/^\s+runs-on:\s*//')
+  [ "$runs_on" = "ubuntu-latest" ] && pass "$wf runs on ubuntu-latest" || fail "$wf runs on '$runs_on'"
+  grep -qE '^\s+timeout-minutes: [0-9]+' "$wf" && pass "$wf sets timeout-minutes" || fail "$wf has no timeout-minutes"
+done
+
+# 2. Triggers are unchanged.
+grep -q 'types: \[opened, synchronize\]' .github/workflows/pr-review.yml \
+  && pass "pr-review triggers on opened and synchronize" || fail "pr-review trigger changed"
+grep -q 'types: \[created\]' .github/workflows/rerun-review.yml \
+  && grep -q "startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')" .github/workflows/rerun-review.yml \
+  && pass "rerun-review triggers on /rereview comments" || fail "rerun-review trigger changed"
+
+# 3. Both workflows open the check run, start the review with the routine settings, and always complete the check run.
+for wf in .github/workflows/pr-review.yml .github/workflows/rerun-review.yml; do
+  grep -q 'run: scripts/check_run.sh open' "$wf" && pass "$wf opens the check run" || fail "$wf does not open the check run"
+  grep -B1 'run: scripts/check_run.sh complete' "$wf" | grep -q 'if: always()' \
+    && pass "$wf always completes the check run" || fail "$wf does not always complete the check run"
+  grep -A7 'run: scripts/start_review.sh' "$wf" | grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: ${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}' \
+    && grep -A7 'run: scripts/start_review.sh' "$wf" | grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}' \
+    && pass "$wf passes the routine URL and token to the start step" || fail "$wf does not pass the routine URL and token to the start step"
+done
+
+# 4. Scripts the workflows run directly are executable in git, so a fresh checkout can run them.
+for script in scripts/check_run.sh scripts/start_review.sh tests/cloud_review_test.sh; do
+  mode=$(git ls-files -s "$script" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+  [ "$mode" = 100755 ] && pass "$script is executable in git" || fail "$script has git mode '$mode'"
+done
+
+# The start script bounds its wait.
+grep -q -- '--max-time' scripts/start_review.sh && pass "start_review.sh bounds the wait" || fail "start_review.sh has no --max-time"
+
+# 5. The start script calls the routine, maps its status codes, and never runs a local reviewer.
+scratch=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -r -- "$scratch"' EXIT
+mkdir "$scratch/bin"
+printf '#!/bin/bash\ntouch "%s/reviewer-ran"\nexit 0\n' "$scratch" > "$scratch/bin/reviewer"
+chmod +x "$scratch/bin/reviewer"
+

+  local url=$1
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=$url CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token REVIEW_MODEL=test-model REVIEW_EFFORT=high \

+if [ -s "$scratch/record.json" ] \

+    "$scratch/record.json" > /dev/null; then
+  pass "request carries the bearer token, pull_request, model and effort"

+"""Stand-in for the cloud routine. Records each request and answers with FAKE_STATUS."""
+import http.server
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+
+status = int(os.environ["FAKE_STATUS"])
+record_path = os.environ["FAKE_RECORD"]
+port_path = os.environ["FAKE_PORT_FILE"]
+
+
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
+        body = self.rfile.read(length).decode()
+        with open(record_path, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b'{"note":"fake routine"}')
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(port_path, "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_address[1]))
+sys.stdout.flush()
+server.handle_request()

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+[[ $pull_request_number =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "bad pull request number: $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2; }

+  [[ $value =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || { echo "bad model or effort: $value" >&2; exit 2; }

+body=$(mktemp)
+trap 'rm -f -- "$body"' EXIT

+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \

+  200) exit 0 ;;
+  422) echo "reviewer reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "cloud routine failed" >&2; exit 1 ;;

+#!/bin/bash

+# Usage: scripts/test_cloud_review.sh [path-to-cloud_review.sh]
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+script=${1:-$root/scripts/cloud_review.sh}
+fails=0
+fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
+
+# Exit code for each routine response, with a stub curl on PATH.
+stub=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -r -- "$stub"' EXIT
+cat > "$stub/curl" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_DIR/args"
+[ "$STUB_STATUS" = "neterr" ] && { printf '000'; exit 28; }
+out=
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do [ "$1" = "-o" ] && out=$2; shift; done
+echo '{"stub":true}' > "$out"
+printf '%s' "$STUB_STATUS"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$stub/curl"
+expect() {
+  STUB_DIR=$stub STUB_STATUS=$1 PATH="$stub:$PATH" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/run CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret-token \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=model-x REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$script" 42 > "$stub/out" 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  [ "$got" = "$2" ] || fail "status $1: exit $got, want $2"
+}
+if [ -f "$script" ]; then
+  expect 200 0
+  expect 422 1
+  expect 500 1
+  expect 401 1
+  expect neterr 1
+  expect 200 0
+  grep -qx 'Authorization: Bearer secret-token' "$stub/args" || fail "bearer header missing"
+  grep -qx '{"pull_request":42,"model":"model-x","effort":"high"}' "$stub/args" || fail "JSON body wrong"
+  grep -qx 'https://routine.example/run' "$stub/args" || fail "routine URL missing"
+  grep -q 'secret-token' "$stub/out" && fail "token printed to log"
+else
+  fail "missing $script"
+fi
+
+# Workflows: cloud only, same triggers, check run kept.
+wf=$root/.github/workflows

+  grep -q 'scripts/check_run.sh open ' "$f" || fail "$f does not open the check run"
+  grep -q 'scripts/check_run.sh complete ' "$f" || fail "$f does not complete the check run"
+  grep -q 'if: always()' "$f" || fail "$f lacks if: always() on completion"

+grep -q 'types: \[created\]' "$wf/rerun-review.yml" || fail "rerun-review trigger changed"
+grep -q "startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/rereview')" "$wf/rerun-review.yml" || fail "rerun filter changed"
+[ -e "$root/scripts/start_review.sh" ] && fail "desktop start_review.sh still present"
+
+[ "$fails" = 0 ] && echo "PASS" || { echo "$fails failure(s)"; exit 1; }

I have a plan. A separate verifier agent checked my reading of the repo and found no errors. It checked my first draft of the plan and found two gaps, around queuing reviews and around testing. The plan below fixes both gaps, but no verifier has checked the revised version yet.

## What the repo tells us

- Both workflows run on the desktop runner and call `scripts/start_review.sh` (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8`, `.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml:9`).
- The cloud session's proxy blocks writes to GitHub's check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:5`). So the workflow must keep opening and completing the `ai-review` check. Branch protection requires that check (`notes/findings.md:7`).
- The routine call waits up to 30 minutes. It returns 200 when the review passed and 422 when it found blocking issues. Any other status means the routine failed (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
- All cloud reviews share one reviewer sign-in. Two reviews refreshing it at the same time can sign one out (`notes/findings.md:4`). "Both exited 0" in finding 1 does not show that both reviews posted comments.
- The NAS runner can make the HTTP call but cannot run the reviewer (`README.md:23`).
- The App private key has only ever been used on the desktop (`notes/findings.md:6`). Any new runner that mints the token is a new place the key gets used.

## Plan

1. **Write the eval first.** Create `scripts/call_routine.sh` and a check that runs it against a local stub server. The stub returns 200, 422 and 500, and also hangs. The check confirms:
   - the bearer token is sent;
   - the JSON body is right (`pull_request` as a number, plus `model` and `effort`);
   - the conclusion is `success` for 200 and `failure` in every other case.

   The check must fail on today's step, which calls the `reviewer` CLI.

2. **Swap the step in both workflows.** Replace "Start reviewer" with `scripts/call_routine.sh`. It posts to `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` with `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. It reads the HTTP status with `curl -w '%{http_code}'` and sets `--max-time` to about 31 minutes. Set the job's `timeout-minutes` to 35. Keep the checkout, App token and check-run steps.

3. **Set the conclusion explicitly.** Today the conclusion comes from `job.status`, so a timeout shows as `cancelled`. Pass the conclusion from step 2 instead, so a timeout or routine error shows as `failure`.

4. **Fix two check-run problems in `scripts/check_run.sh`:**
   - `complete` POSTs a second check run and leaves the first one stuck at `in_progress` (lines 11–12). Have `open` save the run's ID, and have `complete` PATCH that run.
   - `open-for-pr` and `complete-for-pr` each look up the head commit again. A push during the 30-minute wait would complete the check on a different commit. Look up the commit once, at open time.

5. **Run only one review at a time.** Run the review job on one dedicated runner on the NAS, for example labels `[self-hosted, nas, review]`. Jobs waiting for a busy runner stay queued, so no review is lost. Also add a per-PR `concurrency` group shared by both workflows: `ai-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. A newer push then replaces only a queued review of an older commit of the same PR.

   A GitHub-wide concurrency group is the wrong tool here. It cancels older queued runs, and a cancelled run means no check, so branch protection blocks that PR.

6. **Prove it on a test PR.** Run both the `opened` path and `/rereview`, once with a 200 result and once with a 422. For each run, confirm:
   - the review comments were posted;
   - the `ai-review` conclusion matches the result;
   - branch protection accepts the check.

   Then run the same test on the desktop path, and quote both results under "Proof in practice". Never run both paths on the same PR at once, because both write `ai-review`.

7. **Retire the desktop path** after both workflows pass. Remove `scripts/start_review.sh` and the `desktop` label, and update the README tables.

## Decisions for you

- **Where the App key may be used.** Step 5 assumes the NAS. A GitHub-hosted runner would also be a new place for the key, and it has no single-runner queue, so it would need a separate lock.
- **Who may run `/rereview`.** Today anyone who can comment can start one (`.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml:8`). With the cloud routine, each one is a paid outside call. I suggest limiting it to members of the repo.
- **Reviews started outside these workflows.** They also use the shared sign-in, and step 5 does not stop them overlapping. If that happens, the routine itself needs a lock, or each session needs its own sign-in.

Most links in `.claude/rules/index.md` lead to guides that are not in the repo. Only `.claude/docs/rule-guides/verified-work.md` exists, so I followed the other rules from their one-line summaries.

**Basis.** I read the whole repository. A separate verifier agent then checked my research and a first draft of this plan against the files. It confirmed all seven research claims. It marked the serialization step (step 3 in my draft) as a GAP, and I changed that step. Nobody checked GitHub, the NAS, or the routine live, so the plan rests only on what the files say.

### What stays the same and what changes
- **The check run stays in GitHub Actions.** The cloud proxy blocks writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). The workflow keeps creating the App token and opening and closing `ai-review`.
- **The review itself moves to the cloud routine.** The routine is started with an HTTP POST that waits up to 30 minutes. It returns `200` when the review passes and `422` when it finds blocking problems. It posts the review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- **The job runs on the NAS runner `[self-hosted, nas]`.** The NAS can run short jobs and HTTP calls (`README.md:23`), which is all the job needs now.

### Steps
1. **Write the eval first** in `tests/cloud_review_test.sh`. It runs the new script against a local stub server. The stub checks the bearer token and the JSON fields. It has these cases:
   - `200` must exit 0.
   - `422`, `500`, a refused connection, and a hang must each exit 1.
   - The eval must fail before the script exists.
   - A wrong version of the script that maps `422` to 0 must fail the eval.
   - Undoing the script must make the eval fail again.
2. **Add `scripts/cloud_review.sh`.**
   - It builds the body `{pull_request, model, effort}` with `jq`.
   - It reads `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` from the environment and never prints the token.
   - It sends the POST with `curl -w '%{http_code}'` and no `--fail`. The time limit is about 31 minutes, and the eval can lower it with an environment variable.
   - It exits 0 on `200`. On `422`, on any other status, and on a curl error it logs the cause and exits 1. `ai-review` then ends as `failure`, so branch protection blocks the merge (`findings.md:5`).
3. **Change both workflows.**
   - Change `runs-on` to `[self-hosted, nas]`.
   - Replace the "Start reviewer" step with `cloud_review.sh`. Pass it `vars.REVIEW_MODEL`, `vars.REVIEW_EFFORT`, the routine URL, and the token.
   - Put `timeout-minutes: 32` on the review step and about 40 on the job. A step timeout lets the `always()` "Complete check run" step still run. A job timeout would cancel it and leave `ai-review` stuck `in_progress`.
   - Add a concurrency group for each PR at job level, for example `ai-review-${{ PR number }}`. Set `cancel-in-progress: true` so a new push replaces the review of the old commit. Use job level in `rerun-review.yml` so comments other than `/rereview` do not join the group.
4. **Fix how `check_run.sh` closes the check run.** Today "complete" POSTs a second `ai-review` run, and the first run stays `in_progress` (`scripts/check_run.sh:11-12`). For a rerun, it also reads the head SHA again at the end (`:5-7`), so a push during the review moves the result to a different commit. The fix: save the check-run ID and the SHA when the run opens, then PATCH that run when it closes. I include this step because the required check depends on it. You can drop it.
5. **Proof on a test PR**, with the desktop runner still online:
   - A clean PR ends with `ai-review` passing.
   - A PR built to trigger a blocking finding ends with `422` and `failure`.
   - A forced routine error ends with `failure`.
   - `/rereview` writes its result to the correct SHA.
   - Quote the old path and the new path under "Proof in practice".
6. **Clean up after the proof passes.** Run `git rm scripts/start_review.sh`. Update `README.md:5-7`, `:16` and `:22`. Retire the `desktop` runner. Until this step, rolling back means reverting step 3.

### Decisions I need from you
- **The App key moves to a new host.** The key has only ever been used from the desktop (`findings.md:4`). Should it run on the NAS? The other option is a GitHub-hosted runner. Either way, do you want to rotate the key or restrict that runner?
- **Is the sign-in saved between cloud sessions?** The routine docs only say the sign-in is "seeded at setup" (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`). If each session starts from that seed, every review could fail once the first refresh is due, about 10 days in. That risk is larger than two refreshes colliding. The routine owner has to answer this. I recommend you get the answer before cutover.
- **Serializing all reviews.** I left it out. GitHub keeps only one pending run per concurrency group and cancels the older pending one. A cancelled PR would get no `ai-review` and could not merge until someone commented `/rereview`. Two reviews that started at the same moment both passed (`findings.md:1`). If refresh collisions still matter to you, the routine is the place to fix them.
- **Who can trigger `/rereview`.** Any commenter can start it today (`rerun-review.yml:8`), and each run now spends a routine run. Should I add an `author_association` check?

## Steps

1. **Write the test first.** Add a re-runnable test of `scripts/start_review.sh` against a local stub server. The stub has five cases:

   - `422` must exit 1.
   - `500` must exit 1.
   - A refused connection must exit 1.
   - A hang must exit 1.

2. **Rewrite `scripts/start_review.sh`.** Keep the same name and argument, so the workflow steps barely change.

   - Set `--max-time` to about 31 minutes. Do not use `-f`. Capture `%{http_code}` and save curl's exit code, so `set -e` cannot stop the script before it reads the status.
   - Map `200` to exit 0, `422` to exit 1, and any other result to exit 1 with its own log line.
   - Do not use `--retry`. A retry could post a second review.

   - Pass `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` to the start step.
   - Keep the app-token step and both `check_run.sh` steps. The existing `always()` step still turns the job result into the check conclusion.

4. **Add a concurrency group per PR, at job level.**
   - Use `group: ai-review-<PR number>` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. The number comes from `github.event.pull_request.number` in one file and `github.event.issue.number` in the other.
   - The group must sit at job level, under the `if`. At workflow level, every ordinary PR comment would join the group.
   - Do not cancel in progress. Cancelling the job does not stop the cloud routine: the routine keeps running and still posts comments, and a late `cancelled` result can land on the new SHA.
   - With this setting, one review runs and only the newest waits. An older waiting run is dropped before it opens a check, so it leaves no stuck check.

   - The review App has no IP allow list that blocks the NAS. The key has only been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`).

   - A PR with a blocking finding fails and branch protection blocks merge.

+"""Stub cloud routine for tests/start_review_test.sh.
+
+Usage: stub_routine.py PORT_FILE REQUEST_LOG
+Answers each POST with the status named by the request path (/200, /422, /500).
+The path /hang never answers. Each request is appended to REQUEST_LOG as JSON.
+"""
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
+
+port_file, request_log = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+
+
+class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        with open(request_log, "a") as log:
+            log.write(json.dumps({
+                "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                "body": json.loads(body),
+            }) + "\n")
+        if self.path == "/hang":
+            time.sleep(60)
+            return
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(port_file, "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_address[1]))
+server.serve_forever()

# Plan: run PR reviews on the cloud routine

## What I found

- Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]`. Each one mints an App token, opens the `ai-review` check run, runs `scripts/start_review.sh`, and then completes the check (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8`, `.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml:9`).
- The routine starts on a POST to `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and holds the connection open for up to 30 minutes. It returns `200` when the review passes and `422` when there are blocking findings. Any other status means it failed. It posts the review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md`).
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). So the routine cannot report the check itself. An Actions job must keep doing it.
- Concurrent reviews share one reviewer sign-in. If two of them refresh it at the same moment, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:1-2`).
- `scripts/check_run.sh:11-12` has two bugs that exist today:
  - "complete" creates a second check run (POST) and does not update the first one (PATCH). Every review leaves an `in_progress` run behind.
  - `complete-for-pr` looks up the head SHA again at the end. If someone pushes during a `/rereview`, the old review's result lands on the new commit.

A separate verifier agent checked these points. It confirmed all of them against the files and the GitHub docs source.

## Steps

1. **Move the runner.** Change `runs-on` in both workflows to `ubuntu-latest`. Keep the App token step and the check-run steps. Add `timeout-minutes: 40`.
   - The NAS is the other option. But `README.md:23` says the NAS is for short jobs, and this call holds a connection open for 30 minutes.
   - GitHub-hosted runners bill that idle wait if the repo is private.
2. **Add `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh`.** Build the JSON body `{pull_request, model, effort}` with `jq`. POST it with the bearer token and a default `--max-time 1860`, which an environment variable can override.
   - Map `200` to success and `422` to failure. Map any other status, or a timeout, to failure, with its own log message. Never map an error to `neutral`, because a `neutral` result satisfies a required check.
   - Do not retry. Each POST runs a full review that posts comments.
   - Keep the token out of logs (no `curl -v`).
3. **Fix `check_run.sh`.** Save the check run id that `open` returns as a step output, and PATCH that id on completion. In `rerun-review`, look up the head SHA once and use it for both steps.
4. **Control concurrency.**
   - Give both workflows the same per-PR group, keyed on `github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number`, with `cancel-in-progress: true`. A newer push then replaces an older review.
   - Give the job a global group with `queue: max`, so reviews run one at a time and none is dropped. This removes the sign-in refresh race from findings 1–2.
   - Put the `rerun-review` groups at job level. Otherwise any PR comment would cancel a running review.
   - Do not use a global group with the default queue. It silently drops pending reviews of other PRs, and their required check never appears.
5. **Limit who can run `/rereview`.** Add an `author_association` check (OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR) to the `if:` in `rerun-review.yml:8`. Today anyone who can comment can start a review that runs with the secrets.
6. **Make the cutover reversible.** Add a repo variable `REVIEW_BACKEND=cloud|desktop` that selects the runner and the reviewer step. Keep `start_review.sh` until the cloud path has run cleanly for a week or two. Then remove the desktop path, `start_review.sh`, and the desktop row in the README.
7. **Write the eval before the change** (red first).
   - Run the new script against a local stub server that returns 200, 422, 500, and a hang (using a short max-time). Check each result.
   - Put a stub `gh` on PATH that records each call. Check that completion sends one PATCH to the saved id, with the same SHA as the open step.
   - Run the wrong twin (map 500 to success) and an undo of each fix. Both must fail.
8. **Prove it live** before the PR. Run one review on a test PR with the desktop path and one with the cloud path, so the 30-minute held connection is tested for real. Quote both runs under "Proof in practice".

## Questions for you before I build

1. Is `ai-review` pinned to the review App in branch protection? If so, we must keep the App token. `GITHUB_TOKEN` would block merges.
2. Does the App key, or anything else, have an IP allow list? GitHub-hosted runner IPs change. Finding 4 says the key has only ever been used from the desktop.
3. Does the routine stop when the client disconnects? If not, a cancelled job still posts comments.
4. Can the routine take a head SHA? Without one, a push just before the routine starts gets credit for a review of the previous commit.
5. Does the desktop reviewer use the same sign-in as the cloud session? If so, stop desktop reviews when you switch `REVIEW_BACKEND` to cloud.

# Plan: move PR reviews to the cloud routine

## What decides the design
- **The check run stays in GitHub Actions.** The cloud session's proxy blocks writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). So the Actions job still opens and closes `ai-review`, and only the reviewer step moves to the cloud.
- **The job moves to the NAS runner.** The NAS can make HTTP calls but can't run the reviewer (`README.md:23`). A POST to the routine is an HTTP call.
- **Pass/fail stays strict.** `ai-review` must pass before merge (`notes/findings.md:5`). A `200` reply means pass. A `422` reply, any other status, or a timeout means failure (`docs/cloud-routine.md`).

## Steps
1. **Write the test first.** Add `scripts/test_cloud_review.sh`. It points the new script at a fake local endpoint and covers four cases: `200` should exit 0, while `422`, `500` and a timeout should exit non-zero. It also checks the URL, the `Authorization: Bearer` header and the JSON keys `pull_request`, `model` and `effort`. The timeout length can be set, so the test stays short. Run it before the script exists to show it fails.
2. **Add `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh`.** It builds the JSON body with `jq` from the PR number, `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`. It sends a POST to `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` with `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` and never prints the token. The request timeout is about 31 minutes. It exits 0 only on `200`, and its log separates "blocking findings" (`422`) from "routine failed" (anything else).
3. **Change both workflows.**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]`.
   - Replace the "Start reviewer" step with the new script, give it `timeout-minutes: 35`, and pass the URL and token in.
   - Keep the app-token, open and complete steps as they are. `job.status` still sets the check result.
4. **Fix the head SHA in `rerun-review.yml` (needed for this move).** Today `open-for-pr` and `complete-for-pr` each look up the head SHA when they run (`scripts/check_run.sh:5-12`). If someone pushes during the review, a pass can land on a commit nobody reviewed. A 30-minute blocking call makes that window wider. Look up the SHA once in its own step, then pass it to `open` and `complete`.
5. **Limit overlapping runs.**
   - Add a concurrency group per PR at job level (`ai-review-<PR number>`) with `cancel-in-progress: true`. A newer push replaces the older run, so no PR is left without its required check.
   - A single shared group was the first idea, and I dropped it. GitHub keeps only one waiting job per group, so a third trigger cancels the second, which could belong to another PR. That job never starts, never posts `ai-review`, and the PR stays blocked.
   - The sign-in refresh clash (`notes/findings.md:2`) happens inside the cloud session. Ask the routine's owner to handle it there, by queueing refreshes or retrying when a session is signed out. Concurrent reviews already worked in the trials (`notes/findings.md:1`).
6. **Optional: restrict `/rereview`.** Today anyone who comments `/rereview` starts a cloud run (`rerun-review.yml:8`). Allowing only `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR` stops anyone from burning routine runs.

## Checks before merging
- Variable `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and secret `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` exist (`gh variable list`, `gh secret list`). `REVIEW_APP_ID` should be a variable and `REVIEW_APP_KEY` a secret.
- The NAS has `gh`, `jq` and `curl`, can run node actions, and can reach the routine URL.
- The App key has only ever been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). Do a `workflow_dispatch` dry run on the NAS that mints a token and creates a real check run.
- The NAS can tie up a runner slot for up to 30 minutes per review.
- Proof: one PR reviewed with the old setup and one with the new, both quoted under "Proof in practice".

## Switching over
1. Wait until no desktop review job is running.
2. Merge the whole change at once.
3. Pause the desktop runner or remove its `desktop` label. Old workflow files can still send jobs to it, and a desktop review on the same sign-in brings back the refresh clash.
4. Don't use the desktop reviewer sign-in after the switch.
5. To roll back, revert the change and turn the runner back on.
6. Update `README.md` (lines 5–7, 16, 22–23) and `docs/cloud-routine.md`.

## Known limits I'm not fixing
- The routine reviews by PR number, so it reviews whatever the head commit is when it runs. If it can accept a SHA, pass one.
- `complete` creates a second check run instead of updating the first, so each review leaves a stale `in_progress` run behind. This is harmless today, and a small follow-up fixes it.
- PRs from forks get no secrets, so the review fails for them, the same as now.

## Questions for you
1. Can the routine's owner handle the sign-in refresh inside the cloud session?
2. Do you want `/rereview` restricted (step 6)?

# Plan: move PR reviews to the cloud routine

## What I found

- Both workflows run on the desktop runner and call `scripts/start_review.sh`. That script runs the reviewer CLI locally (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8,21`, `rerun-review.yml:9,22`, `scripts/start_review.sh:4-8`).
- The cloud routine starts with one POST and waits up to 30 minutes for the review. It returns `200` when the review passes, `422` when it has blocking findings, and any other code when the routine itself failed. The routine posts the review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). So a GitHub Actions runner must still mint the App token and open and complete the `ai-review` check.
- Branch protection requires `ai-review` (`notes/findings.md:5`). Every path must end in a completed check, including failure and cancellation.
- The NAS runner is always on and can make HTTP calls (`README.md:23`). It becomes the runner for these workflows.
- Two reviews at once worked on the shared sign-in. The risk is two sign-in refreshes at the same moment, which happens about every 10 days and can sign one session out (`notes/findings.md:1-2`).
- The App private key has only ever been used on the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). Moving to the NAS uses it from a new host.
- There is an existing bug in `rerun-review`. The complete step reads the head SHA again at the end (`scripts/check_run.sh:12`). If someone pushes during the review, the old SHA keeps a check stuck in progress, and the new SHA gets a result for code that was never reviewed.
- `open` and `complete` each create a new check run instead of updating one (`scripts/check_run.sh:9-12`). Each review therefore leaves two `ai-review` runs on the SHA.

## Steps

1. **Add `scripts/fire_routine.sh`.**
   - Build the JSON body with `jq` from the PR number, `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`.
   - POST it to `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`. Pass the bearer header through `--config` or `-H @-` so the token does not show in `ps` on the NAS.
   - Use `--max-time 1860`, and read the status with `-w '%{http_code}'`.
   - A `200` exits 0. A `422` exits 1 with the message "blocking findings". Any other code, a curl transport error, or a timeout (curl exit 28) exits 1 with the message "routine failed".
2. **Change both workflows.**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]` and `timeout-minutes: 35`.
   - Replace the "Start reviewer" step with `fire_routine.sh`, passing `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` as env.
   - Keep the app-token step, the open step, and the `if: always()` complete step on the runner.
3. **Fix the check-run handling.**
   - Resolve the head SHA once at the start of `rerun-review` and use it for both open and complete.
   - Save the id of the opened check run and PATCH that run on complete, so each review leaves one run.
   - Show which outcome happened in the check summary: blocking findings or routine failure.
4. **Add per-PR concurrency.** Use the group `ai-review-<PR number>` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, shared by both workflows. A new push or a `/rereview` then replaces the older run. Cancelling the runner job does not stop a cloud routine that is already running. That routine still posts its comments, on the older SHA.
5. **Roll out in stages.**
   - Switch `rerun-review` first, because it runs less often. Test it.
   - Then switch `pr-review`.
   - Keep the desktop runner as a fallback until both pass.
   - Then remove `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm`, and update `README.md` lines 5-7, 16 and 22.

## Checks before calling it done

- A clean test PR gives `200`, and the check shows success with comments posted.
- A PR with a planted blocking issue gives `422`, and the check shows failure.
- A bad token gives another status code. The check still completes, as a failure.
- Cancelling a run mid-review still leaves a completed check.
- A push during `/rereview` sends the result to the SHA resolved at the start.
- The first App token mint on the NAS succeeds.
- All of the above pass with the desktop runner stopped.

## Decisions for you

1. **Refresh race.** One global concurrency group would make reviews run one at a time. GitHub allows only one pending run per group, though, and a new pending run cancels the older one ([GitHub docs: concurrency](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/using-concurrency)), so reviews could be dropped. My recommendation: keep per-PR groups only, and put a refresh lock inside the cloud routine, outside this repo.
2. **App key on the NAS.** Do you accept that the key will now be used from the NAS?
3. **NAS tools.** Nothing in the repo shows that `gh`, `curl` and `jq` are installed on the NAS. Please confirm they are.
4. **`/rereview` access.** Any commenter can trigger it (`rerun-review.yml:8`). With the routine, each trigger spends the cloud token. Should it be limited to members and collaborators?

A separate verifier agent checked the findings and the plan. It confirmed all eight findings. It marked every plan step SOUND except the checks list, which was missing tests. I added those tests above (cancellation, push mid-review, first key use, comments), so the revised list has not been checked again. Per the repo rules, each check also needs a fresh verifier run once the work is built.

The plan follows. I have not edited any files. A separate verifier has not checked this plan yet, as the repo's verified-work rule requires, so treat it as a draft.

# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop runner to the cloud routine

## What the repo says

- **Today:** Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]`. Each one gets an App token, opens the `ai-review` check, runs `scripts/start_review.sh` (the local `reviewer` CLI), then completes the check (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`, `rerun-review.yml`).
- **The routine:** You start it with a POST to `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, using the bearer token `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. The body is `{pull_request, model, effort}`. The call waits up to 30 minutes, then returns `200` for a pass, `422` for blocking findings, and any other status for a failure. The routine posts the review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md`).
- **Limits from `notes/findings.md`:**
  - The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (#3), so the routine cannot set the check.
  - Branch protection requires `ai-review` (#5).
  - The App key has only been used from the desktop (#4).
  - All reviews share one reviewer sign-in. Running two at once worked (#1), but two refreshes at the same moment can sign one session out (#2).
- **The NAS runner** `[self-hosted, nas]` is always on and handles short jobs and HTTP calls (`README.md`).

## The design

GitHub Actions keeps control of the check run. The routine only runs the review. Each workflow job moves to the NAS, gets the App token, opens the check, calls the routine, and completes the check based on the HTTP status.

## Steps

1. **Add `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh <pr_number>`.**
   - It POSTs the JSON body with `curl --max-time 1860` (just over 30 minutes) and keeps the HTTP status.
   - It exits 0 on `200`.
   - It exits 1 on `422` and prints "blocking findings".
   - It exits 1 on any other status and prints the status and response body, so a broken routine also fails the check.
   - It reads `REVIEW_MODEL`, `REVIEW_EFFORT`, `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` from env, with `:?` guards like the current script.
   - It builds the body with `jq -n` to avoid quoting problems. Step 7 confirms `jq` and `curl` are on the NAS.

2. **Change both workflows.**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]`.
   - In the "Start reviewer" step, call `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh` and pass `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL: ${{ vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL }}` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}`.
   - Add `timeout-minutes: 40` to the job.
   - Keep the token, open-check and complete-check steps as they are. The same App and the same check name keep branch protection (#5) satisfied, and the App token lasts 1 hour, which covers the 30-minute call.

3. **Prevent duplicate reviews of one PR.**
   - Add `concurrency: { group: ai-review-<PR number>, cancel-in-progress: true }` to both workflows. The PR number is `github.event.pull_request.number` in `pr-review.yml` and `github.event.issue.number` in `rerun-review.yml`, so a push and a `/rereview` on the same PR share one group.
   - With this group, a new push cancels the outdated review. The cancelled run still completes its check as `cancelled` because that step has `if: always()`.
   - Do not use one global group. GitHub keeps only one pending run per group and cancels the rest, so other PRs would silently get no `ai-review` check and could not merge.

4. **Handle the sign-in refresh race (#2).** This needs your decision. Steps 1–3 do not fix it. The options are:
   - (a) Accept the risk, because a refresh happens about every 10 days.
   - (b) Add a lock or a single-flight refresh inside the routine.
   - (c) Refresh on a schedule when reviews are quiet.

   I recommend (a) for the cutover and (b) as a follow-up. The routine config is not in this repo, so I cannot plan (b) in detail from here.

5. **Test the App key from the NAS (#4).** Run `actions/create-github-app-token` and one `check_run.sh open` from a NAS job on a test PR before the cutover. The test exercises the key and a check-runs write from the new runner.

6. **Remove the desktop path.**
   - Remove `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm`.
   - Update the README: the workflows table, "Both workflows call…", and the runners table.
   - Point `docs/cloud-routine.md` to the new script.
   - Retire the desktop runner only after step 7 passes.

7. **Verify on real runs.** Record the result of each check.
   - The NAS has `curl` and `jq`, and the repo has the variable and secret.
   - A test PR with a clean change: the routine returns `200`, `ai-review` shows success, and the review comments appear.
   - A test PR with a known blocking issue: the routine returns `422`, `ai-review` shows failure, and merge is blocked.
   - Routine failure: a wrong URL on a branch makes `ai-review` fail and no check stays stuck in progress.
   - `/rereview` on a PR runs and updates the check.
   - Two PRs at once both get a review.
   - The same run on the old workflow (desktop) is the baseline for "Proof in practice" in the PR.

8. **Rollback.** Revert the workflow commit. The desktop runner and `start_review.sh` stay in git history until step 6 is complete.

## Out of scope

- `check_run.sh complete` POSTs a new check run each time and never updates the open one. That is existing behavior and the move does not need to change it.
- Fork PRs do not get repository secrets. That is already true for the App key, so the move does not change it.

## Decisions for you

- Which option for the refresh race in step 4.
- NAS or a GitHub-hosted runner. I recommend the NAS because the README already lists it for HTTP calls. A GitHub-hosted runner works the same way if the NAS should not hold a 30-minute job.

I read every file and had a fresh verifier agent check what I found and a draft plan. It confirmed all eight findings below and flagged four gaps. This version fixes those gaps. I made no edits.

## What the repo shows

- **Today:** Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]` and call `scripts/start_review.sh`, which runs the reviewer on the desktop (`pr-review.yml:8`, `rerun-review.yml:9`).
- **Cloud routine:** A POST with `pull_request`, `model` and `effort` waits up to 30 minutes. It returns `200` for a pass, `422` for blocking findings, and anything else means the routine failed. The routine posts its own review comments (`docs/cloud-routine.md`).
- **Check runs:** The cloud proxy blocks writes to check runs (finding #3), and branch protection requires `ai-review` (finding #5). A GitHub Actions job must still open and close the check.
- **Runner:** The NAS can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer (`README.md:23`). The App key has only ever been used from the desktop (finding #4).
- **Sign-in:** Two reviews at once both exited 0. The risk is two sessions refreshing the sign-in at the same moment, which can sign one out (findings #1, #2).
- **Existing bugs the move should fix:**
  - `check_run.sh complete` creates a second check run and leaves the `in_progress` one open forever (`check_run.sh:11-12`).
  - `rerun-review` looks up the head SHA twice, so a push during a review splits the check across two commits.

## Plan

1. **Write the check first.** Add a test that runs a new `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh` against a local stub server.
   - Cases: `200`, `422`, `500`, and a timeout. Make the time limit an env setting so the timeout case runs fast.
   - It also checks the request: the bearer header and the JSON fields and their types.
   - It must fail now, because the script does not exist yet. A script that treats `422` as a pass, or uses `curl -f`, must also fail it.
2. **Add `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh`.**
   - Build the body with `jq`, sending `pull_request` as a number and taking `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT` with `${…:?}`.
   - Read the status with `curl -sS -o body -w '%{http_code}'` and `--max-time` of about 1900 seconds.
   - Exit 0 on `200`. Exit 1 on `422`, logging "blocking findings". Exit with its own code on any other status or a timeout (`000`), logging "routine failed: <code>".
   - Never turn on `set -x`, because it would print the token.
3. **Fix `check_run.sh`.** `open` prints the check-run id, and `complete` PATCHes that id. Drop `open-for-pr` and `complete-for-pr`.
4. **Change both workflows.**
   - `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]` and `timeout-minutes: 35`.
   - Keep the App token step.
   - Replace the reviewer step with `start_cloud_review.sh`, passing `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`, `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`.
   - Close the check only if the open step succeeded.
   - In `rerun-review`, look up the head SHA once and pass it on through `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
   - Change both workflows in one commit, so the desktop and the cloud never review at the same time.
5. **Before cutover, confirm on the NAS:**
   - The App token mints there.
   - `gh`, `jq` and `curl` are installed.
   - The NAS can reach the routine URL.
   - The URL variable and token secret exist. This clone has no remote, so I could not check them.
   - Then run a trial on one PR that hits both the pass path and the blocking path.
6. **Rollback and cleanup.** Keep `start_review.sh` and the desktop runner until a review passes after the ~10-day sign-in refresh. Mark that date at cutover. Then remove the desktop path and update `README.md` lines 5-7, 16, 22-23.

## Decision for you

How should cloud reviews avoid the sign-in refresh race?
- **(a) Serialize them through one NAS runner.** Jobs queue and none are dropped. **I recommend this, if there is only one NAS runner.**
- **(b) A GitHub concurrency group per PR at job level.** This cancels reviews of stale commits but still allows reviews of different PRs at the same time.
- **Avoid a single repo-wide concurrency group.** It throws away queued runs. A dropped run never opens its `ai-review` check, so that PR cannot merge.

Two facts I could not settle: whether the cloud sign-in shares refresh state with the desktop's, and whether the routine can review a specific SHA rather than the latest commit on the PR.

## Not in scope, flagged only

- Anyone who can comment can trigger `/rereview`. An `author_association` check would limit that.
- PRs from forks get no secrets, so the required check never appears on them. This is already true today.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs cloud_review.sh against a local stub of the cloud routine.
+set -uo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+port=18765
+python3 -c '
+import http.server, json, sys
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
+        ok = (self.headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer t0ken"
+              and body == {"pull_request": 42, "model": "m", "effort": "high"})
+        code = int(self.path.strip("/")) if ok else 400
+        self.send_response(code); self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
+' "$port" &
+server=$!
+trap 'kill $server' EXIT
+sleep 1
+export REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t0ken
+fail=0
+check() {
+  local path=$1 want=$2
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/$path" "$here/cloud_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then echo "ok   HTTP $path -> exit $got"; else echo "FAIL HTTP $path -> exit $got, want $want"; fail=1; fi
+}
+check 200 0
+check 422 1
+check 500 1
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:1/200" "$here/cloud_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+[ $? = 1 ] && echo "ok   unreachable -> exit 1" || { echo "FAIL unreachable"; fail=1; }

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine and waits for its result (docs/cloud-routine.md).
+# Exit 0: review passed (200). Exit 1: blocking findings (422). Exit 2: the routine failed.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1

+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \

+status=$(printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" | curl -sS -o "$response" -w '%{http_code}' \
+  --max-time 1860 \
+  -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+  -H @- \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data "$body") || status=000
+cat "$response"; echo

+  200) echo "Review passed." ;;
+  422) echo "Reviewer reported blocking findings." >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "Cloud routine failed with HTTP $status." >&2; exit 2 ;;
+esac

+json_string() {

+  -X POST "$url" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" \

+  --data "$body" \
+  "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL")
+cat "$response"
+echo
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "review reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
