meta.prior_reply:
# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop to the cloud routine

A fresh verifier agent checked my reading of the repo and a first draft of this plan. Its corrections are included below. Most of the rule guides listed in `.claude/rules/index.md` do not exist in the repo. Only `verified-work.md` is there.

## What sets the design

- **The routine cannot write check runs.** The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:5`). Merging needs a passing `ai-review` check (`notes/findings.md:7`). So the GitHub workflow must keep opening and closing the check run, using the same App token. The routine only runs the review and posts the comments.
- **The NAS can make the call.** The desktop is needed today only for the reviewer CLI (`scripts/start_review.sh`). The cloud routine replaces that step with one blocking HTTP POST (`docs/cloud-routine.md`). The NAS runner can make HTTP calls (`README.md:23`).
- **The routine's replies are known.** It returns 200 when the review passes and 422 when it finds blocking problems. Any other status, or no reply after 30 minutes, means the routine failed.
- **Two notes from the trials.** The App key has only ever been used from the desktop (finding 4). Reviews that run at the same time all succeed, but two sign-in refreshes at the same moment can sign the session out (findings 1 and 2).

## Steps

1. **Check the NAS before any change.**
   - Mint an App token on the NAS with `REVIEW_APP_ID` and `REVIEW_APP_KEY`, and create and update one test check run.
   - Confirm that `gh`, `curl` and `jq` are installed.
   - Confirm that the NAS can reach `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`.
   - Send one manual POST for an open PR.

2. **Add `scripts/request_cloud_review.sh` to replace `start_review.sh`.**
   - Build the body `{pull_request, model, effort}` with `jq`, taking the values from `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`.
   - POST it with the bearer token from `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. Set `--max-time` to about 31 minutes and read the status with `-w '%{http_code}'`.
   - Save curl's exit code before `set -e` can stop the script. Then exit 0 on 200, and exit 1 on 422 with "blocking findings". Exit 1 on a timeout or any other status with "routine failed", so the two failures look different in the log.
   - Do not use `--retry`. A second POST starts a second review, which posts its comments twice.

3. **Change both workflows.**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]` and `timeout-minutes: 40`.
   - Pass `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` to the new script.
   - Keep the App-token steps and the `if: always()` step that completes the check run. A timeout or a cancel still marks the check `cancelled`, so the merge stays blocked.

4. **Fix `scripts/check_run.sh` while it is open (recommended).**
   - Today `complete` creates a second check run and does not update the first one. Each review leaves one run stuck at `in_progress`. Save the `id` that `open` returns and PATCH `check-runs/{id}`.
   - In the `/rereview` path, read the PR's head SHA once and use it for both calls. Today a push during the review can put the open and the complete on different commits.

5. **Set concurrency.** Give each PR its own group with `cancel-in-progress` for `pr-review`, so a new push replaces the old review. Do not use one group for the whole repo. GitHub keeps only one waiting run per group and cancels older waiting runs, so reviews would be lost. A cancel stops only curl, so the routine can still post comments on the old commit. The docs will say so.

6. **Update the docs.**
   - In the README, change the runners section and describe the new flow.
   - In `docs/cloud-routine.md`, add the steps to re-seed the reviewer sign-in after it is signed out.
   - Keep the desktop runner registered for a short rollback window, where undoing the change is one `git revert`. Then remove it.

7. **Prove it on a test PR, then right after the merge.**
   - On the test PR: one review that passes (200), one with blocking findings (422), and one routine failure caused by a bad token. Also run one review that takes close to 30 minutes, to see whether the long HTTP connection stays open. Then push during a review, and open two PRs at the same time.
   - Test `/rereview` only after the merge. `issue_comment` always runs the workflow from the default branch, so before the merge it would still use the desktop.
   - Quote the before and after runs under "Proof in practice" in the PR.

## Decisions for you

1. **How many runners does the NAS have?** A self-hosted runner does one job at a time, so each review holds a runner for up to 30 minutes. With one runner, other NAS jobs wait behind reviews, but reviews never overlap, which also prevents the sign-in refresh race. With two or more runners, reviews can overlap and the race stays possible. My recommendation: add a second runner, accept the small race risk, and rely on step 6's re-seed steps and the clear "routine failed" check result.
2. **Who can start a review with `/rereview`?** Today any commenter can trigger it (`rerun-review.yml:8`), and each one now uses a cloud routine run. I recommend limiting it to `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR` through `author_association`.
3. **Is step 4 in or out?** It fixes problems that exist today, separate from the move. I can put it in this PR or in its own PR.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs the review on the cloud routine (docs/cloud-routine.md) and waits for it.
+# Exit 0: review passed. Exit 1: blocking findings, or the routine failed.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(jq -cn \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+response=$(mktemp)
+trap 'rm -f "$response"' EXIT
+# The token goes in on stdin so it stays out of the process list.
+# No --retry: a second POST starts a second review that posts its comments again.
+curl_exit=0
+status=$(printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" |
+  curl -sS -o "$response" -w '%{http_code}' \
+    --max-time "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_MAX_TIME:-1860}" \
+    -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+    -H @- \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    --data "$body") || curl_exit=$?
+case "$curl_exit:$status" in
+  0:200) echo "Review passed." ;;
+  0:422) echo "Review reported blocking findings." >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *)
+    echo "Cloud routine failed: curl exit $curl_exit, HTTP status ${status:-none}." >&2
+    head -c 2000 "$response" >&2
+    exit 1
+    ;;
+esac

+"""Stand-in for the cloud routine, used by tests/test_scripts.sh.
+
+Usage: stub_routine.py <status|sleep> <log_file> <port_file>
+Replies with the given HTTP status, or never replies for "sleep".
+Each request is appended to log_file as one JSON line.
+"""
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
+
+mode, log_file, port_file = sys.argv[1:4]
+
+
+class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        with open(log_file, "a") as log:
+            log.write(json.dumps({
+                "path": self.path,
+                "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                "body": json.loads(body or b"null"),
+            }) + "\n")
+        if mode == "sleep":
+            time.sleep(30)
+            return
+        self.send_response(int(mode))
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"{}")
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(port_file, "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_address[1]))
+server.serve_forever()

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks scripts/request_cloud_review.sh against a stub routine and
+# scripts/check_run.sh against a stub gh. Run: tests/test_scripts.sh
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill $(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+check() {
+  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then
+    echo "PASS $1"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL $1: expected [$2], got [$3]"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}
+
+# run_review <case> <stub mode>: sets code, out, log for the case.
+run_review() {
+  log="$tmp/$1.log"
+  : > "$log"
+  python3 -I "$repo/tests/stub_routine.py" "$2" "$log" "$tmp/$1.port" &
+  local stub=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$tmp/$1.port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+  out=$(CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$tmp/$1.port")/run" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret-token REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_MAX_TIME=2 \
+    "$repo/scripts/request_cloud_review.sh" 42 2>&1)
+  code=$?
+  kill "$stub" 2>/dev/null
+  wait "$stub" 2>/dev/null
+}
+
+contains() { case "$1" in *"$2"*) echo yes ;; *) echo no ;; esac; }
+
+run_review pass 200
+check "200 exits 0" 0 "$code"
+check "one request sent" 1 "$(wc -l < "$log" | tr -d ' ')"
+check "body" '{"effort":"high","model":"m1","pull_request":42}' "$(jq -cS .body "$log")"
+check "bearer token" "Bearer secret-token" "$(jq -r .authorization "$log")"
+check "json content type" "application/json" "$(jq -r .content_type "$log")"
+check "token not printed" no "$(contains "$out" secret-token)"
+
+run_review blocking 422
+check "422 exits 1" 1 "$code"
+check "422 says blocking findings" yes "$(contains "$out" "blocking findings")"
+
+run_review broken 500
+check "500 exits 1" 1 "$code"
+check "500 says routine failed" yes "$(contains "$out" "routine failed")"
+check "500 not retried" 1 "$(wc -l < "$log" | tr -d ' ')"
+
+run_review timeout sleep
+check "timeout exits 1" 1 "$code"
+check "timeout says routine failed" yes "$(contains "$out" "routine failed")"
+check "timeout not retried" 1 "$(wc -l < "$log" | tr -d ' ')"
+
+# Stub gh: logs its arguments and answers like the GitHub API.
+mkdir -p "$tmp/bin"
+cat > "$tmp/bin/gh" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+echo "$*" >> "$GH_LOG"
+case "$*" in
+  *pulls/*" -q .head.sha") echo abc123 ;;
+  *check-runs/*) echo '{}' ;;
+  *check-runs*" -q .id") echo 9876 ;;
+  *) echo '{"id":9876,"name":"ai-review"}' ;;
+esac
+EOF
+chmod +x "$tmp/bin/gh"
+export GH_LOG="$tmp/gh.log" GITHUB_REPOSITORY=o/r
+gh_run() { : > "$GH_LOG"; PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" "$repo/scripts/check_run.sh" "$@"; }
+
+check "head-sha prints sha" abc123 "$(gh_run head-sha 42)"
+check "open prints check run id" 9876 "$(gh_run open abc123)"
+check "open creates ai-review in progress" yes \
+  "$(contains "$(cat "$GH_LOG")" "check-runs -f name=ai-review -f head_sha=abc123 -f status=in_progress")"
+gh_run complete 9876 failure > /dev/null
+check "complete updates the opened run" "api -X PATCH repos/o/r/check-runs/9876 -f status=completed -f conclusion=failure" "$(cat "$GH_LOG")"
+
+if [ "$failures" -ne 0 ]; then
+  echo "$failures check(s) failed"
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "all checks passed"

# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop to the cloud routine

I read every file in the repository. Two fresh verifier agents checked the work. The research verifier confirmed all 10 claims. The plan verifier found gaps in concurrency, the eval, and the rollout, and this plan includes those fixes. I changed no files. Nobody has run the plan yet.

## What stays and what moves

- **Moves to the cloud:** the review itself. The routine runs `reviewer exec review` and posts the comments (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`).
- **Stays on a GitHub Actions runner:** minting the App token and writing the `ai-review` check run. The cloud proxy refuses check-run writes (`notes/findings.md:3`), and branch protection requires that check (`notes/findings.md:5`).
- **New runner:** `[self-hosted, nas]`. It can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md:23`).

## Steps

1. **Pre-checks on the NAS, before any switch**
   - A job on the NAS mints an App token and calls the GitHub API. This is the first use of the key away from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`).
   - `gh`, `jq` and `curl` are installed.
   - The `nas` runner is registered to this repository.
   - Count the runner processes on the NAS. Step 5 needs that number.
   - The NAS can keep an HTTP request open for 31 minutes.
   - `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` exist.
   - The routine's reviewer sign-in is seeded and valid.
   - A routine run can post PR comments. The notes only show that check-run writes are refused.

2. **New script `scripts/start_cloud_review.sh <pr>`**
   - It POSTs `{pull_request, model, effort}` to `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, taking model and effort from `vars.REVIEW_MODEL` and `vars.REVIEW_EFFORT`.
   - It sends the bearer header through `--config` on stdin, so the token stays off the process list.
   - The timeout is `--max-time ${CLOUD_REVIEW_MAX_TIME:-1860}`, which is 31 minutes by default. The routine can block for 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
   - It reads the status with `-w '%{http_code}'` and maps it: 200 becomes `success`, 422 becomes `failure`, and any other status or a curl error becomes `failure`. The status goes in the log.
   - It writes `conclusion=` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` and exits 0.

3. **Fix `scripts/check_run.sh`**
   - `open` resolves the head SHA once and returns the check-run id.
   - `complete` PATCHes `check-runs/<id>`. Today `complete` POSTs a second run and leaves the first one in progress (`check_run.sh:11-12`).
   - The rerun workflow can no longer complete on a different SHA from the one it opened (`check_run.sh:10,12`).

4. **Both workflows**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]` and `timeout-minutes: 40`.
   - Keep the token and check-run steps.
   - The complete step uses `if: always()` and skips when no check-run id exists.
   - Its conclusion is `steps.review.outputs.conclusion || 'failure'`, so a cancelled or timed-out run fails the check. Today the conclusion is `job.status` (`pr-review.yml:27`, `rerun-review.yml:28`).

5. **Concurrency**
   - Add a job-level group to both workflows: `ai-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}`, with `cancel-in-progress: false`.
   - The group goes at job level because `rerun-review` fires on every comment. At workflow level, an ordinary comment would cancel a pending review for a new push.
   - **Decision for you:** the sign-in refresh race across different PRs (`notes/findings.md:2`). A collision can sign out the shared sign-in, and then every review fails until someone re-seeds it.
   - Option (a): one runner process on the NAS. Reviews then run one at a time, but other NAS jobs can wait up to 31 minutes.
   - Option (b): the routine serializes its own runs.
   - A single global concurrency group does not work. It drops the pending reviews of other PRs.

6. **Limit `/rereview`** to commenters whose `author_association` is OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR. Today anyone can trigger a paid remote run (`rerun-review.yml:8`).

7. **Eval, written before the change**
   - A stub HTTP server returns 200, 422 and 500. A test asserts the script's conclusion for each status.
   - A short `CLOUD_REVIEW_MAX_TIME` tests the timeout. A refused connection tests a curl error.
   - A `gh` shim on `PATH` asserts that `complete` sends a PATCH to `check-runs/<id>`.
   - Run `actionlint` on both workflows.
   - Red/green checks:
     - The tests are red before the change and green after.
     - An inverted mapping fails.
     - Undoing the change fails again.

8. **Rollout**
   - Switch `pr-review` on a test PR. Run one desktop review and one cloud review, one after the other.
   - Do not type `/rereview` on the test PR before the merge. `issue_comment` workflows run from the default branch, so it would start the old desktop path.
   - Merge both workflows.
   - Update `README.md`: lines 5–7, 16, and the runner table.
   - Drain any queued `desktop` jobs, then stop the desktop runner service.
   - Keep the desktop runner registered but stopped for a set period. To roll back, revert the workflow files.
   - Delete `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm`.
   - Write down how to re-seed the routine's sign-in.

## Open items

- **Your decision:** option (a) or (b) in step 5.
- **Missing guides:** `.claude/rules/index.md` links to guides under `docs/rule-guides/`, and that directory does not exist. I followed `.claude/docs/rule-guides/verified-work.md`, which is the only guide in the repository.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud routine for one pull request and waits for the result.
+# Writes conclusion=success|failure to $GITHUB_OUTPUT and exits 0 once the
+# routine has answered or failed. Bad inputs exit non-zero with no
+# conclusion; the workflow then completes the check as failure.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(jq -nc \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+
+# The header goes in on stdin so the token stays off the process list.
+# Escape backslashes and quotes for curl's config syntax.
+token=${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}
+case "$token" in *$'\n'* | *$'\r'*) echo "CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN contains a line break." >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
+token=${token//\\/\\\\}
+token=${token//\"/\\\"}
+status=$(printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$token" |
+  curl --silent --show-error --config - \
+    --max-time "${CLOUD_REVIEW_MAX_TIME:-1860}" \
+    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    --data "$body" \
+    --output /dev/null \
+    --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+    "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}") || status="curl-error-$?"
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) conclusion=success ;;
+  422) echo "The reviewer reported blocking findings." ;&
+  *) conclusion=failure ;;
+esac
+echo "Cloud routine returned $status; conclusion $conclusion."
+echo "conclusion=$conclusion" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?}"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs the review-bot checks. Exits non-zero when any check fails.
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+pass() { echo "PASS $1"; }
+fail() { echo "FAIL $1: $2"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }
+
+# --- start_cloud_review.sh ---------------------------------------------------
+
+# Runs the script against the stub. Args: name status delay max_time expected [port]
+review_case() {
+  local name=$1 status=$2 delay=$3 max_time=$4 expected=$5 port=${6:-}
+  local record=$work/$name.json output=$work/$name.out
+  : > "$output"
+  if [ -z "$port" ]; then
+    port=$((20000 + RANDOM % 20000))
+    timeout 15 python3 -I "$root/tests/stub_routine.py" "$port" "$status" "$delay" "$record" &
+    local stub=$!
+    sleep 0.5
+  fi
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/review" \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token \
+  CLOUD_REVIEW_MAX_TIME=$max_time \
+  REVIEW_MODEL=test-model REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+  GITHUB_OUTPUT=$output \
+    bash "$root/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh" 42 > "$work/$name.log" 2>&1
+  local code=$?
+  [ -n "${stub:-}" ] && wait "$stub" 2> /dev/null
+  local got
+  got=$(sed -n 's/^conclusion=//p' "$output")
+  if [ "$code" -ne 0 ]; then
+    fail "review $name" "script exited $code"
+  elif [ "$got" != "$expected" ]; then
+    fail "review $name" "conclusion '$got', want '$expected'"
+  else
+    pass "review $name"
+  fi
+}
+
+review_case passed 200 0 10 success
+review_case blocking 422 0 10 failure
+review_case routine-error 500 0 10 failure
+review_case timeout 200 3 1 failure
+review_case refused 0 0 10 failure 1
+
+# The request carries the token and the routine contract fields.
+record=$work/passed.json
+if [ -f "$record" ] &&
+  [ "$(jq -r .auth "$record")" = "Bearer test-token" ] &&
+  [ "$(jq -c .body "$record")" = '{"pull_request":42,"model":"test-model","effort":"high"}' ]; then
+  pass "review request"
+else
+  fail "review request" "$(cat "$record" 2> /dev/null || echo 'no request recorded')"
+fi
+
+# A token with a quote or backslash reaches the routine whole.
+port=$((20000 + RANDOM % 20000))
+timeout 15 python3 -I "$root/tests/stub_routine.py" "$port" 200 0 "$work/quote.json" &
+stub=$!
+sleep 0.5
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/review" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN='ab"c\d' \
+  REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e GITHUB_OUTPUT=$work/quote.out \
+  bash "$root/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+wait "$stub" 2> /dev/null
+got=$(jq -r .auth "$work/quote.json" 2> /dev/null)
+[ "$got" = 'Bearer ab"c\d' ] && pass "review token quoting" || fail "review token quoting" "header '$got'"
+
+# A token with a line break is refused before curl runs.
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1/review CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=$'a\nurl = "http://evil"' \
+  REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e GITHUB_OUTPUT=$work/newline.out \
+  bash "$root/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh" 42 > "$work/newline.log" 2>&1
+code=$?
+if [ "$code" -ne 0 ] && ! grep -q conclusion= "$work/newline.out" 2> /dev/null && ! grep -q evil "$work/newline.log"; then
+  pass "review token line break"
+else
+  fail "review token line break" "exit $code: $(cat "$work/newline.log")"
+fi
+
+# The token stays off the command line.
+if grep -q 'CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN' "$root/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh" &&
+  ! grep -E '^[^#]*curl[^#]*\$\{?CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN' "$root/scripts/start_cloud_review.sh" > /dev/null; then
+  pass "review token off argv"
+else
+  fail "review token off argv" "curl line names the token, or the script is missing"
+fi
+
+# --- check_run.sh --------------------------------------------------------------
+
+shim=$work/shim
+mkdir -p "$shim"
+cat > "$shim/gh" << 'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+echo "$*" >> "$GH_LOG"
+case "$*" in
+  *"pulls/7"*) echo abc123 ;;
+  *"--method POST"*"check-runs"*) echo 555 ;;
+esac
+EOF
+chmod +x "$shim/gh"
+export GH_LOG=$work/gh.log GITHUB_REPOSITORY=owner/repo
+
+: > "$GH_LOG"
+sha=$(PATH=$shim:$PATH bash "$root/scripts/check_run.sh" head-sha 7 2> /dev/null)
+[ "$sha" = abc123 ] && pass "check head-sha" || fail "check head-sha" "got '$sha'"
+
+: > "$GH_LOG"
+id=$(PATH=$shim:$PATH bash "$root/scripts/check_run.sh" open abc123 2> /dev/null)
+if [ "$id" = 555 ] && grep -q -- '--method POST repos/owner/repo/check-runs .*head_sha=abc123' "$GH_LOG"; then
+  pass "check open"
+else
+  fail "check open" "id '$id', calls: $(cat "$GH_LOG")"
+fi
+
+: > "$GH_LOG"
+PATH=$shim:$PATH bash "$root/scripts/check_run.sh" complete 555 failure > /dev/null 2>&1
+if grep -q -- '--method PATCH repos/owner/repo/check-runs/555 .*conclusion=failure' "$GH_LOG" &&
+  ! grep -q -- '--method POST' "$GH_LOG"; then
+  pass "check complete"
+else
+  fail "check complete" "calls: $(cat "$GH_LOG")"
+fi
+
+# --- workflows -----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+for wf in pr-review rerun-review; do
+  file=$root/.github/workflows/$wf.yml
+  if grep -q 'runs-on: \[self-hosted, nas\]' "$file" &&
+    ! grep -q 'desktop' "$file" &&
+    grep -q "steps.review.outputs.conclusion || 'failure'" "$file" &&
+    grep -q '^    concurrency:' "$file" &&
+    grep -q 'start_cloud_review.sh' "$file" &&
+    grep -q 'ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}' "$file" &&
+    grep -q '\[ -n "$id" \]' "$file"; then
+    pass "workflow $wf"
+  else
+    fail "workflow $wf" "not on the NAS cloud path"
+  fi
+done
+
+if grep -q 'author_association' "$root/.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml"; then
+  pass "rerun author check"
+else
+  fail "rerun author check" "any commenter can start a review"
+fi
+
+if command -v actionlint > /dev/null; then
+  if actionlint -shellcheck= "$root"/.github/workflows/*.yml; then pass actionlint; else fail actionlint "see output"; fi
+else
+  echo "SKIP actionlint (not installed)"
+fi
+
+echo "$failures failure(s)"
+[ "$failures" -eq 0 ]

+"""Stub cloud routine for tests.
+
+Usage: stub_routine.py <port> <status> <delay_seconds> <record_file>
+Answers one POST with <status> after <delay_seconds>, and writes the
+Authorization header and the request body to <record_file>.
+"""
+import http.server
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+
+port, status, delay, record = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), float(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4]
+
+
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        with open(record, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        time.sleep(delay)
+        try:
+            self.send_response(status)
+            self.end_headers()
+        except BrokenPipeError:
+            pass
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler).handle_request()

meta.prior_reply:
# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop runner to the cloud routine

Two fresh verifier agents read the repo and checked my research and a first draft of this plan. Both only read files, and nothing was run. Their corrections are folded in below.

## What sets the design

- Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]` and call `scripts/start_review.sh` (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8,21`, `.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml:9,22`).
- You start the routine with a blocking POST that waits up to 30 minutes. It returns `200` when the review passes and `422` when it has blocking findings. Any other status means the routine failed. The routine posts the review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- The cloud cannot write check runs (`notes/findings.md:5`). So the GitHub Actions job keeps opening and completing the `ai-review` check, which branch protection requires (`notes/findings.md:7`).
- The NAS runner can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer (`README.md:23`). It can host a job that only sends the POST and waits.
- The App key has only ever been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:6`). Minting a token on the NAS will be its first use there.
- Two reviews at once worked (`notes/findings.md:3`). Two sign-in refreshes at once can sign a session out (`notes/findings.md:4`).

## Steps

1. **Add `scripts/fire_routine.sh <pr>`.**
   - It builds the JSON body with `jq` and POSTs it with the bearer token.
   - It exits 0 on `200`, 1 on `422` and 2 on anything else, including a timeout.
   - It records curl's exit code itself, so that `set -e` does not stop the script before it maps a timeout.
   - The time limit comes from `ROUTINE_MAX_TIME`, default 1860 seconds.
   - The log says "blocking findings" or "routine failed", because both cases end as `failure`. Neither case ends as `neutral`: GitHub counts a `neutral` required check as passing.
   - The script never prints the token.
2. **Change both workflows.**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]`.
   - Replace the "Start reviewer" step with `fire_routine.sh`, with `timeout-minutes: 35` on that step and 40 on the job. The `if: always()` complete step then still runs.
   - Keep the app-token step and `actions/checkout`, which provides the scripts. The same App then still creates `ai-review`.
3. **Fix the check-run handling in `scripts/check_run.sh`.**
   - Every action is a POST, so "complete" creates a second `ai-review` run and the first one stays open (`scripts/check_run.sh:9-12`). Change `open` to return the run ID and `complete` to PATCH that run.
   - In the rerun workflow, look up the head SHA once and pass it to both steps. Today a push during the 30-minute window splits open and complete (`scripts/check_run.sh:10,12`).
4. **Add a per-PR concurrency group.** Use `concurrency: { group: ai-review-<pr number>, cancel-in-progress: false }`. I dropped my first idea of one global group. GitHub keeps only one pending run per group and cancels older pending runs, so a third PR would get no `ai-review` result and could not merge.
5. **Check the NAS before cutover.**
   - It has `gh`, `curl` and `jq`.
   - The App token mints there, which may need the NAS address on an App or org IP allow list.
   - It has enough runners that a job held for 30 minutes does not block other NAS work.
6. **Cover the sign-in risk.** Someone must refresh the cloud sign-in on a schedule while no review runs. No file says who does this today (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`). This replaces serializing all reviews.
7. **Cut over in one PR.**
   - Let the desktop runner's queue empty first, so that a desktop review and a cloud review never use the shared sign-in at the same time.
   - Keep `start_review.sh` until the live proof passes, so a revert is the full rollback.
   - In a follow-up PR, remove `start_review.sh`, update the README tables and deregister the desktop runner.
8. **Eval first, as the repo rules require.**
   - Write a re-runnable test that runs `fire_routine.sh` against a local stub server.
   - The stub returns 200, 422 and 500, and stalls past `ROUTINE_MAX_TIME=2`. The expected exit codes are 0, 1, 2 and 2.
   - The stub also checks the bearer header and the `pull_request`, `model` and `effort` fields, and checks that the token never appears in the output.
   - The test fails before step 1 exists. A wrong twin that maps 422 to 0 also fails.
   - Live proof: a clean PR gets `ai-review` success. A PR with a planted bug gets failure. `/rereview` works. Three PRs opened at once each get a conclusion.

## Known gaps I would not fix in this change

- A cancelled or timed-out job probably leaves the cloud review running, so it can still post comments. I would document this.
- Anyone can comment `/rereview` (`rerun-review.yml:8`), and each comment now starts a cloud run. An `author_association` check would close this.
- PRs from forks get no secrets, so the required check fails for them. This was also true on the desktop.

## Decisions for you

- **Sign-in refresh (step 6):** who runs it, and how often? The notes say a refresh is needed about every 10 days. They do not say whether an idle sign-in expires.
- **`/rereview` limit:** should I add the `author_association` check now?
- **Check-run fix (step 3):** this bug also exists today. Should it go in the cutover PR or a separate one?

+"""Stand-in for the cloud routine endpoint, used by tests/test_fire_routine.sh.
+
+Usage: stub_routine.py <mode> <port_file> <record_file>
+mode is an HTTP status to return, or "stall" to never answer in time.
+Writes the chosen port to port_file and the first request to record_file.
+"""
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
+
+mode, port_file, record_file = sys.argv[1:4]
+
+
+class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
+        body = self.rfile.read(length).decode()
+        with open(record_file, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({
+                "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                "body": body,
+            }, f)
+        if mode == "stall":
+            time.sleep(30)
+            return
+        self.send_response(int(mode))
+        self.end_headers()
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(port_file, "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_port))
+server.handle_request()

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/fire_routine.sh (or the script given as $1) against a local stub
+# of the cloud routine and checks the exit code for each routine response.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+script=${1:-$repo/scripts/fire_routine.sh}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+export NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1 no_proxy=127.0.0.1
+token=test-token-5f3a9c
+failures=0
+
+run_case() {
+  local mode=$1 expected=$2
+  local port_file=$work/port.$mode record=$work/record.$mode out=$work/out.$mode
+  python3 "$repo/tests/stub_routine.py" "$mode" "$port_file" "$record" &
+  local stub=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$port_file" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+  local code=0
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$port_file")/" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=$token REVIEW_MODEL=test-model REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    ROUTINE_MAX_TIME=2 bash "$script" 17 >"$out" 2>&1 || code=$?
+  kill "$stub" 2>/dev/null; wait "$stub" 2>/dev/null
+
+  local problems=()
+  [ "$code" = "$expected" ] || problems+=("exit $code, want $expected")
+  if [ -s "$record" ]; then
+    [ "$(jq -r .authorization "$record")" = "Bearer $token" ] || problems+=("bad Authorization header")
+    [ "$(jq -r .content_type "$record")" = "application/json" ] || problems+=("bad Content-Type")
+    [ "$(jq -c '.body | fromjson' "$record")" = '{"pull_request":17,"model":"test-model","effort":"high"}' ] \
+      || problems+=("bad body: $(jq -r .body "$record")")
+  else
+    problems+=("routine received no request")
+  fi
+  ! grep -q "$token" "$out" || problems+=("token printed")
+
+  if [ ${#problems[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
+    echo "PASS $mode -> exit $code"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL $mode: ${problems[*]}"; sed 's/^/  | /' "$out"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}
+
+run_case 200 0
+run_case 422 1
+run_case 500 2
+run_case stall 2
+
+[ "$failures" -eq 0 ] && echo "all cases passed" || { echo "$failures case(s) failed"; exit 1; }

# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop to the cloud routine

## What the repo shows

- Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]`. They mint an App token, open the `ai-review` check, run `scripts/start_review.sh`, and complete the check (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`, `.github/workflows/rerun-review.yml`).
- The cloud routine starts with an HTTP POST and holds the connection until the review ends, for up to 30 minutes. It returns `200` when the review passes, `422` when it finds blocking issues, and any other status when the routine itself fails. It posts the review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md`).
- The cloud session's proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md` #3). So the check run must stay on a GitHub Actions runner. The cloud only runs the review.
- The NAS runner can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md`). That fits this split.
- Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md` #5). Any status other than `200` must therefore leave the check failed.

## Steps

1. **Write the check first.** Add `scripts/test_call_routine.sh`. It replaces `curl` with a stub and asserts how each response maps to a check conclusion: `200` → `success`, `422` → `failure`, `500` → `failure`, timeout or no connection → `failure`. Run it before step 2 and confirm it fails (red).

2. **Add `scripts/call_routine.sh <pr-number>`.** It POSTs `{"pull_request", "model", "effort"}` to `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` with `Authorization: Bearer $CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. It sets `curl --max-time` to about 1900 s, just above the routine's 30-minute limit. It prints the conclusion and exits non-zero for every status except `200`. It builds the body with `jq -n` so that no `$(...)` lands in a workflow line. The test from step 1 must now pass.

3. **Change both workflows.**
   - Set `runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]` and `timeout-minutes: 35`.
   - Replace the "Start reviewer" step with `scripts/call_routine.sh`. Pass `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` from `vars` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` from `secrets`. Keep `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`.
   - Keep the App token step and both check-run steps on the runner. The `if: always()` completion stays, so a failed call still completes the check with `failure`.
   - Add `concurrency: { group: ai-review-${{ PR number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`. This stops a new push and an older review on the same PR from racing. Finding #1 shows that parallel reviews across different PRs work on one sign-in.

4. **Fix the head SHA in `rerun-review`.** `open-for-pr` and `complete-for-pr` each look up the head SHA separately (`scripts/check_run.sh`). If someone pushes during the 30-minute wait, the check opens on one SHA and completes on another, and the first check stays `in_progress`. Look up the SHA once in a first step and pass it to `open` and `complete`. The `*-for-pr` actions are then unused. Propose removing them.

5. **Delete `scripts/start_review.sh`** with `git rm`. Update the README's workflow note and runner table: the desktop is no longer used.

6. **Cut over safely.** Test on one PR while the desktop runner is still registered. Unregister the desktop runner only after `200`, `422`, and `/rereview` all behave correctly on real PRs.

## Risks to settle before or during the build

- **Sign-in refresh race** (finding #2). A sign-out makes the routine return a non-`200` status. The check then fails closed, and `/rereview` recovers. If the routine can refresh the sign-in on a schedule, run the refresh at a quiet hour. I could not find out from the repo whether it can. Please tell me, or check the routine settings.
- **NAS holds a job for up to 30 minutes.** The README describes the NAS as a place for "short jobs." The job only waits on a socket. If the NAS runs one job at a time, though, reviews will queue behind each other. Check its runner concurrency. A GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner is the fallback.
- **App private key on a new host** (finding #4). The key stays an Actions secret, but the NAS will be the first host other than the desktop to use it. Decide whether to rotate the key at cutover.
- **The routine posts comments through the proxy.** Finding #3 only names check runs as blocked. The step-6 trial confirms comments arrive.
- **`/rereview` from any commenter** now triggers a paid cloud run. Consider limiting it with `github.event.comment.author_association` to `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, or `COLLABORATOR`.
- **Repo settings.** I have not confirmed that `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` exist in the repo settings. Check with `gh variable list` and `gh secret list` before step 3.

## Verification status

No separate verifier has checked this plan yet. The repo's verified-work rule asks for one before building. I can run that check next, then implement.

+  *) printf '%s' "$STUB_STATUS" ;;

+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire

+export REVIEW_EFFORT=high

+failures=0

+    echo "ok   $status -> $want"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL $status -> want $want, exit $got"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}

+expect 200 pass
+expect 422 fail
+expect 500 fail
+expect 401 fail
+expect timeout fail
+expect refused fail
+
+STUB_STATUS=200 "$here/call_routine.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+want_body='{"pull_request":42,"model":"model-x","effort":"high"}'
+got_body=$(grep -A1 -x -- '--data-binary' "$STUB_ARGS" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | jq -c . 2>/dev/null)

+if grep -qx 'header = "Authorization: Bearer secret-token"' "$STUB_BODY" 2>/dev/null; then echo "ok   bearer"; else echo "FAIL bearer"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi

+max_time=$(grep -A1 -x -- '--max-time' "$STUB_ARGS" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2)

+for bad in 'ab"cd' 'ab\cd' $'ab\ncd'; do

+    echo "FAIL token with special character accepted"; failures=$((failures + 1))
+  else
+    echo "ok   token with special character refused"
+  fi
+done
+

# Plan: run PR reviews on the cloud routine

Two separate verifier agents checked this plan. The first confirmed all ten facts it rests on. The second found gaps in concurrency, sign-in serialization and the eval. The plan below includes those fixes. The repo has no remote, so I could not check anything on live GitHub: runners, branch protection, variables, secrets or App settings.

## Constraints from the notes

- The routine posts its own review comments. The POST waits up to 30 minutes. A `200` means the review passed, a `422` means blocking findings, and anything else means the routine failed (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). The `ai-review` check run must therefore still be opened and completed from a runner.
- Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`).
- If two sessions refresh the shared sign-in at once, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:2`). Calls to the routine should run one at a time.
- The NAS runner can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md:23`).

## Pieces

**1. New script `scripts/call_routine.sh`**
- POST the JSON body `{pull_request, model, effort}` to `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` with the bearer token `$CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. Build the body with `jq --argjson` so the PR number is a JSON number.
- Read the status with `curl -w '%{http_code}'` and no `--fail`. Check curl's own exit code separately.
- Exit codes:
  - `200`: exit 0.
  - `422`: exit 1 with the message "blocking findings".
  - Any other status, or a curl error: exit 1 with "routine failed: <status>".
- Check the required variables with `:?`, as `start_review.sh` does.
- Set the curl timeout to about 31 minutes. An environment variable can override it so the test can use a few seconds.

**2. Edit both workflows**
- Change `runs-on` to `[self-hosted, nas]` and set `timeout-minutes: 35`.
- Replace the "Start reviewer" step with `call_routine.sh`. Its env comes from `vars.REVIEW_MODEL`, `vars.REVIEW_EFFORT`, `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`.
- Keep the App token step and the open and complete check-run steps unchanged. The complete step keeps `if: always()`, so a timeout or cancel still completes the check.

**3. Concurrency per PR**
- Put the group at the job level, so ordinary PR comments do not enter it. The key is `pr-review-<PR number>`, shared by both workflows.
- Set `cancel-in-progress: false`. Cancelling a job only stops curl. The cloud session keeps running, so a new run would start a second session and post duplicate comments.
- Do not add a global group. GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so queued reviews would be dropped.

**4. Sign-in refresh race**
- Require exactly one runner with the `nas` label. One runner runs one job at a time, so routine calls run one at a time.
- A sign-out shows as a failed check with the "routine failed" message.
- Add a re-seed runbook and the one-runner requirement to `docs/cloud-routine.md`.
- A lock inside the routine would be stronger, if the owner can add one.

**5. Eval, written before piece 1**
- A shell test runs `call_routine.sh` against a local stub HTTP server. Cases: `200`, `422`, `500`, a hang (short timeout) and a refused connection.
- It checks exit codes, messages, the bearer header and the JSON body the stub received.
- It must fail before the script exists. It must also fail on a wrong twin, such as a script that exits 0 on `422`, and fail again when the script is reverted.

**6. Live trial**
- Before merge, on a test PR: one passing review and one review with blocking findings. Confirm the `ai-review` conclusion each time, and confirm that branch protection blocks the merge on the blocking PR.
- After merge, run a `/rereview` trial. GitHub runs `issue_comment` workflows from the default branch, so until the merge, `/rereview` still uses the desktop. Keep the desktop runner registered until this trial passes.
- For the pull request, record runs with and without the change under "Proof in practice".

**7. Docs and cleanup**
- Update the README prose and tables: lines 5-7, line 16 and the runner rows.
- After the trial passes, remove `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm`.
- Unregister the desktop runner.

## To confirm before building

- `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` exist in the repository.
- The NAS:
  - Has `curl`, `jq` and `gh`, and a runner version that runs node20 actions.
  - Can reach the routine URL, and no proxy drops a connection that stays idle for 30 minutes.
  - Has exactly one runner with the `nas` label. Also find out which other jobs would wait behind a 30-minute review.
- The App token works from the NAS. The key has only been used from the desktop, so check for an IP allow list.
- Find out whether branch protection pins `ai-review` to the review App.

## Out of scope; worth a separate decision

- `check_run.sh complete` creates a second check run instead of updating the first.
- Anyone who can comment can trigger `/rereview`. After the move, each trigger costs a cloud run.

I edited no files.

+"""Stub cloud routine for tests/call_routine_test.sh.
+
+Usage: stub_routine.py <status|hang> <port-file> <request-file>
+Writes the bound port to <port-file>, records the first request's
+Authorization header and body to <request-file>, then answers with
+<status>, or never answers when given "hang".
+"""
+import http.server
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+
+mode, port_file, request_file = sys.argv[1:4]
+
+
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        with open(request_file, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({
+                "path": self.path,
+                "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                "body": body.decode(),
+            }, f)
+        if mode == "hang":
+            time.sleep(60)
+            return
+        self.send_response(int(mode))
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"{}")
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(port_file, "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_address[1]))

I have a plan, but no `verifier` agent has checked it yet, as `.claude/docs/rule-guides/verified-work.md` requires. Treat it as a draft.

## What the repository says

- Both workflows run on the owner's desktop (`[self-hosted, desktop]`). Each one gets a GitHub App token, opens the `ai-review` check, runs `scripts/start_review.sh`, and then closes the check (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`, `rerun-review.yml`).
- The cloud routine is started by an HTTP POST to `vars.CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL`, with the token in `secrets.CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. The body carries `pull_request`, `model` and `effort`. The routine posts the review comments itself. The POST can take up to 30 minutes. It returns `200` when the review passes and `422` when there are blocking findings. Any other status means the routine failed (`docs/cloud-routine.md`).
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API, so the routine cannot open or close the `ai-review` check (`notes/findings.md` #3).
- Branch protection needs `ai-review` to pass before a merge (#5). Each pull request still needs exactly one check that ends in a final state.
- Two reviews can run at the same time without trouble (#1). The shared sign-in refreshes about every 10 days, and two refreshes at the same moment can sign one session out (#2).
- The NAS runner can make short jobs and HTTP calls. It cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md`).

## Plan

1. **Keep check handling in GitHub Actions.** Getting the token and opening and closing the check stay in the workflow, through `scripts/check_run.sh`, which needs no changes. Only the review step moves to the cloud. This is required by finding #3.

2. **Replace the review step with a call to the routine.** Add `scripts/trigger_cloud_review.sh <pr>`. The script does these things:
   - It sends the POST with curl. The bearer token comes from an env var, never from the command line. The body is built with `jq` from `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`.
   - It sets `--max-time` a little above 30 minutes, for example 1900 s.
   - It turns the HTTP status into an exit code and a conclusion: `200` gives `success`, `422` gives `failure`, and any other status gives `failure` and prints the response body to the log.
   - It drops `--post-comments`, because the routine posts the comments itself.

   Then remove `scripts/start_review.sh`.

3. **Move both workflows to a runner without the reviewer CLI.** Change `runs-on` to `[self-hosted, nas]`, or to `ubuntu-latest` if hosted minutes are acceptable. Add `timeout-minutes: 40` so a stuck job still lets the `always()` step close the check. The NAS is described as running "short jobs", so confirm it can hold one 30-minute HTTP call. If it cannot, use a hosted runner.

4. **Run reviews one at a time.** Put both workflows in one shared group, for example `concurrency: { group: ai-review-cloud, cancel-in-progress: false }`. This stops two sign-in refreshes from happening at once (finding #2).
   - There is a trade-off: GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so a third run that arrives would cancel the waiting one.
   - A cancelled job never opens its check. For a `pull_request` run, the newer push still gets reviewed. For a `/rereview` run, the user comments again. The merge stays blocked until then, so nothing merges without a review.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud routine for one pull request and waits for the review.
+# Exit 0: review passed (200). Exit 1: blocking findings (422). Exit 2: routine failed.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
+
+jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}' > "$work/payload"
+# The token goes through a file so it stays out of the process list.
+printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" > "$work/headers"
+
+status=$(curl -sS -X POST \
+  --max-time 1900 \
+  -H @"$work/headers" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data-binary @"$work/payload" \
+  -o "$work/body" \
+  -w '%{http_code}' \
+  "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}") || true
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "Review passed." ;;
+  422) echo "Review reported blocking findings."; exit 1 ;;
+  *)
+    echo "Cloud routine failed with HTTP status ${status:-none}." >&2
+    [ -s "$work/body" ] && cat "$work/body" >&2
+    exit 2 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Eval for scripts/trigger_cloud_review.sh. A stub curl stands in for the
+# cloud routine and answers with the status in FAKE_STATUS.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
+
+mkdir "$work/bin"
+cat > "$work/bin/curl" <<'STUB'
+#!/bin/bash
+out=/dev/null
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$FAKE_DIR/argv"
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    -o) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
+    --data) printf '%s' "$2" > "$FAKE_DIR/payload"; shift 2 ;;
+    --data-binary) cat "${2#@}" > "$FAKE_DIR/payload"; shift 2 ;;
+    -H)
+      case "$2" in
+        @*) cat "${2#@}" >> "$FAKE_DIR/headers" ;;
+        *) printf '%s\n' "$2" >> "$FAKE_DIR/headers" ;;
+      esac
+      shift 2 ;;
+    *) printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$FAKE_DIR/args"; shift ;;
+  esac
+done
+if [ "$FAKE_STATUS" = 000 ]; then printf '000'; exit 28; fi
+printf 'routine said %s' "$FAKE_STATUS" > "$out"
+printf '%s' "$FAKE_STATUS"
+STUB
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl"
+
+failures=0
+run_case() {
+  local status=$1 want_exit=$2
+  rm -f "$work"/payload "$work"/headers "$work"/args "$work"/argv
+  PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" FAKE_DIR="$work" FAKE_STATUS="$status" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/run CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok123 \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$repo/scripts/trigger_cloud_review.sh" 42 > "$work/log" 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  if [ "$got" -ne "$want_exit" ]; then
+    echo "FAIL status $status: exit $got, want $want_exit"; cat "$work/log"; failures=$((failures + 1)); return
+  fi
+  echo "ok   status $status -> exit $got"
+}
+
+run_case 200 0
+run_case 422 1
+run_case 500 2
+run_case 401 2
+run_case 000 2
+
+# The payload and headers of the last HTTP call must match docs/cloud-routine.md.
+run_case 200 0
+want='{"pull_request":42,"model":"m1","effort":"high"}'
+got=$(jq -c . "$work/payload" 2>/dev/null)
+if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then echo "ok   payload $got"; else echo "FAIL payload: got '$got', want '$want'"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+if grep -qx 'Authorization: Bearer tok123' "$work/headers" 2>/dev/null; then echo "ok   bearer header"; else echo "FAIL bearer header missing"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi

# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop runner to the cloud routine

I read every file in the repository. A separate verifier agent checked my findings and the draft plan against the files. It confirmed all eight findings. It found gaps in the draft's test list and found several missing details, and I added them below. This plan is not verified in practice: the repository has no remote, so I could not see repository variables, runners, or GitHub state.

## Facts the plan depends on

- Both workflows run on `[self-hosted, desktop]` and run the reviewer locally through `scripts/start_review.sh` (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml:8,21`, `rerun-review.yml:9,22`).
- The NAS runner can make HTTP calls. It cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md:23`).
- You start the routine with a POST. The call waits for up to 30 minutes. It returns 200 when the review passes and 422 when the reviewer reports blocking findings. Any other status means the routine failed. The routine posts the review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API, so the GitHub workflow must keep opening and completing the check runs (`notes/findings.md:3`).
- Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass, so no failure path can report success (`notes/findings.md:5`).
- The App private key has only been used from the desktop runner (`notes/findings.md:4`).
- Concurrent reviews worked in the trials. If two sessions refresh the shared sign-in at the same moment, one session can be signed out. The refresh happens about every 10 days (`notes/findings.md:1-2`).

## Steps

1. **Prepare the NAS runner.** Confirm that `gh`, `curl`, and `jq` are installed, because `check_run.sh` calls `gh`. Confirm that the `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` variable and the `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` secret exist. Mint one App token on the NAS to test the key on that runner for the first time.

2. **Split each workflow into two jobs on `[self-hosted, nas]`.**
   - Job `open`: it is outside any concurrency group. It mints the App token, gets the head SHA, opens the `ai-review` check run, and outputs the SHA.
   - Job `review`: it has `needs: open`, its own App token, and `timeout-minutes: 35`. The token cannot pass between jobs because GitHub drops job outputs that hold secrets.

3. **Replace "Start reviewer" with a call to the routine.** Build the body `{pull_request, model, effort}` with `jq` from `vars.REVIEW_MODEL` and `vars.REVIEW_EFFORT`. POST it with `curl --max-time 1860` and save the HTTP status. Do not let `set -e` stop the step before the status is saved.

4. **Complete the check run with an explicit result.** 200 gives `success`. 422, any other status, an empty status, a timeout, or a curl error gives `failure`. This step replaces `job.status` at `pr-review.yml:27` and `rerun-review.yml:28` and keeps `if: always()`.

5. **Fix the SHA in `/rereview`.** Complete the check run on the SHA that job `open` output. Today `complete-for-pr` gets the head SHA again at the end (`check_run.sh:12`). A push during the 30-minute call can then put the result on the wrong commit.

6. **Serialize the calls to the routine.** Put job `review` in one concurrency group that both workflows share, with `cancel-in-progress: false`. This prevents the sign-in refresh race. GitHub keeps only one pending run per group and cancels the older ones. A cancelled run leaves its check run `in_progress`, so merge stays blocked and `/rereview` recovers it.
   **Decision for you:** with three or more reviews in 30 minutes, some reviews are dropped and nobody is told. The other choice is no concurrency group: the trials show that parallel reviews work, and you accept the refresh race about every 10 days.

7. **Clean up.** Delete `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm`, because the two workflows are its only callers. In `check_run.sh`, remove `open-for-pr` and `complete-for-pr` if job `open` now gets the SHA. Update `README.md:5-7,16,22`.

8. **Roll out.** Merge the change. GitHub runs `issue_comment` workflows from the default branch, so `/rereview` uses the old desktop path until the merge. Remove the desktop runner only after both paths pass on real PRs.

## Checks before the work counts as done

Each check must fail on the old state, pass on the new state, and fail again when the fix is undone.

- A normal PR gets `ai-review` = success, and the routine's comments appear on it. Nothing yet shows that the cloud proxy allows comment writes.
- A PR that gets 422 shows `failure`. The docs do not say how to force a 422, so ask the routine owner, or use a PR with a planted blocking bug.
- A wrong token or URL, and a forced curl timeout, each show `failure`. They never show success, and the completion step still runs.
- Two PRs opened together run one after the other. A cancelled pending run leaves `ai-review` `in_progress`.
- After the merge, `/rereview` works on the NAS. A push during a rerun leaves each result on the correct SHA. To test before the merge, add a `workflow_dispatch` trigger.

## Out of scope, noted

- `check_run.sh` creates a new check run each time it is called and never updates the open one (`check_run.sh:9-12`). This works today. A later cleanup could PATCH the open run by its ID.
- Anyone who can comment can start `/rereview` (`rerun-review.yml:8`), and that run uses the repository secrets.
- The docs do not say whether `pull_request` is a number or a URL (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The plan sends the number.

To proceed, I need your choice on step 6. After that I can make the changes.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs the review on the cloud routine and prints the check-run conclusion.
+set -uo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(jq -n --argjson pr "$pull_request_number" --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pr, model: $model, effort: $effort}') || exit 1
+# The token goes in on stdin so it does not show in the process list.
+status=$(printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" |
+  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1860 -X POST \
+    -H @- \
+    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    --data "$body" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}")
+curl_exit=$?
+echo "cloud routine returned HTTP ${status:-none}, curl exit $curl_exit" >&2
+if [ "$curl_exit" -eq 0 ] && [ "$status" = 200 ]; then
+  echo success
+else
+  echo failure
+fi

+#!/bin/bash
+# Stands in for curl in tests/call_routine_test.sh.
+# It prints FAKE_STATUS as the HTTP code when the request matches what the
+# cloud routine expects, and 000 otherwise.
+set -uo pipefail
+auth="" body="" url=""
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    -H) if [ "$2" = @- ]; then auth=$(cat); else [[ "$2" == Authorization:* ]] && auth=$2; fi; shift 2 ;;
+    --data) body=$2; shift 2 ;;
+    -o|-w|-X|--max-time) shift 2 ;;
+    -*) shift ;;
+    *) url=$1; shift ;;
+  esac
+done
+if [ -n "${FAKE_CURL_EXIT:-}" ]; then
+  printf '%s' "${FAKE_STATUS:-000}"

+if [ "$auth" != "Authorization: Bearer $EXPECT_TOKEN" ] || [ "$url" != "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL" ] || [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
+  echo "fake curl: unexpected request auth=[$auth] url=[$url] body=[$body]" >&2
+  printf 000
+  exit 1
+fi

I read every file in the repository. Two fresh verifier agents then checked the work. The research verifier confirmed all 10 claims. The plan verifier marked 4 pieces as GAP, and the plan below includes those fixes. I ran nothing against GitHub or the cloud routine.

# Plan: move PR reviews to the cloud routine

## Constraints from the repo
- **Check-run writes stay in Actions.** The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). The GitHub Actions job must open and complete the check run.
- **The check name stays `ai-review`.** Branch protection requires it to pass before merge (`notes/findings.md:5`).
- **How the routine works.** One POST waits up to 30 minutes. It returns `200` when the review passes and `422` for blocking findings. Any other status means the routine failed. The routine posts its own review comments (`docs/cloud-routine.md:5-7`).
- **One shared sign-in.** Reviews running at the same time worked, but two refreshes at the same moment can sign a session out (`notes/findings.md:1-2`).

## Steps
1. **Runner.** Move both jobs to `[self-hosted, nas]`. The NAS mints the App token, opens and completes the check run, and sends the POST. No runner needs the reviewer CLI any more. Two catches: the review holds the NAS for up to 30 minutes, which blocks its other short jobs, and the App key would be used from a new host (step 1 under "Decisions for you").
2. **New `scripts/fire_routine.sh <pr>`.**
   - It builds the body with `jq`: `pull_request`, `model` from `REVIEW_MODEL`, and `effort` from `REVIEW_EFFORT`. It also sends `head_sha` if the routine accepts it.
   - It POSTs with `curl --max-time 1860` and reads the token from an environment variable, so the token does not show in the process list.
   - It maps the result: `200` → `success`, `422` → `failure`, anything else → `failure` with the log line `routine failed (HTTP N)`.
   - It writes `conclusion` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` before it exits, so a curl timeout cannot skip that write.
3. **Remove `scripts/start_review.sh`** with `git rm`. Its `--post-comments` would post the comments a second time.
4. **Fix `scripts/check_run.sh`.**
   - `open` writes the check-run id to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
   - `complete` sends `-X PATCH` to `check-runs/{id}`. Today it POSTs a second run, so every PR ends up with two `ai-review` runs (`check_run.sh:11-12`).
   - The rerun job looks up the head SHA once and passes it to both steps. This removes `open-for-pr` and `complete-for-pr`, which can land on different commits if someone pushes during a review.
5. **Complete step.** It keeps `if: always()`. It uses the conclusion from step 2, reports `cancelled` when the job is cancelled, and falls back to `failure` in every other case.
6. **Concurrency and timeout.**
   - Each job gets `timeout-minutes: 40`.
   - Each job gets the group `ai-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. A started review cannot be cancelled in the cloud, so it runs to the end and only the newest waiting review stays queued.
   - The group goes at job level, under the `/rereview` `if`. At workflow level, the routine's own comments would trigger and cancel reviews.
7. **Refresh race.** If the NAS has only one runner process, reviews queue and run one at a time. That removes the refresh race without a global group, which would drop waiting runs. First check how many runner processes the NAS has.
8. **Who can run `/rereview`.** Check the commenter through `repos/.../collaborators/{user}/permission`, since each run now starts a paid cloud review. Today any commenter can trigger it (`rerun-review.yml:8`).
9. **README.** Update the opening paragraph, the line "Both workflows call `scripts/start_review.sh`", the Runners table, and the NAS "Use" column.

## Verification (before any done claim)
1. **Local test.** Run `fire_routine.sh` against a stub server that returns `200`, `422`, `500`, and a timeout. Check the conclusion and the exit code. The test must fail against a wrong mapping first, then pass.
2. **Before cutover.** Confirm that `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` exist in the repository.
3. **Live test pull requests:**
   - A clean change. Expect `success`, comments posted once, and exactly one `ai-review` run.
   - A change with a planted blocking issue. Expect `failure`.
   - A push during a review. Expect the newer review to run after the first one, with no duplicate comments.
   - `/rereview` from someone with write access. Expect a review.
   - `/rereview` from someone without write access. Expect it to be ignored.
4. **Desktop runner.** It stays registered until all of these pass. Then it is removed.
5. **Shipping.** Load `pr-lifecycle` before committing. Quote the runs with and without the change under "Proof in practice".

## Decisions for you
1. **App key on the NAS.** Do you accept using the App private key from the NAS? So far it has only been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). The alternative is a GitHub-hosted runner.
2. **One review at a time.** Do you accept slower throughput to remove the refresh race?
3. **Expired sign-in.** An expired sign-in would fail every review and block every merge. Do you want an alert or a runbook for re-seeding the sign-in?

Fork pull requests get no secrets, so their reviews fail to mint a token. That is already true today, and this plan leaves it as it is.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine (docs/cloud-routine.md) and waits for it.
+# Writes conclusion=success|failure to $GITHUB_OUTPUT and exits nonzero
+# unless the review passed.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+: "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}"
+

+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "$REVIEW_MODEL" \
+  --arg effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+
+# The token goes in on stdin so it stays out of the process list.
+status=$(printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" |
+  curl --silent --show-error --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+    --max-time "${ROUTINE_MAX_TIME:-1860}" \
+    --header @- \
+    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    --data-binary "$body" \
+    "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL") || true
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) conclusion=success; echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) conclusion=failure; echo "review reported blocking findings" ;;
+  *) conclusion=failure; echo "routine failed (HTTP ${status:-none})" >&2 ;;
+esac
+echo "conclusion=$conclusion" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+[ "$conclusion" = success ]

+"""Stub cloud routine for tests/fire_routine_test.sh.
+
+Usage: stub_routine.py <port-file> <request-log> <status|sleep>
+Answers every POST with <status>, or sleeps 30 seconds when given "sleep".
+Writes the request headers and body to <request-log>.
+"""
+import http.server
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+
+port_file, request_log, mode = sys.argv[1:4]
+
+
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        with open(request_log, "w") as log:
+            json.dump({
+                "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                "body": json.loads(body or b"null"),
+            }, log)
+        if mode == "sleep":
+            time.sleep(30)
+            return
+        self.send_response(int(mode))
+        self.end_headers()
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(port_file, "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_address[1]))
+server.serve_forever()

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \

# Plan: move PR reviews from the desktop runner to the cloud routine

A verifier agent checked all 8 research claims against the files and confirmed them. A second verifier checked the draft plan: P1–P4 passed and P5–P7 had gaps. I revised P5–P7 below, and no verifier has checked the revised versions yet.

## Constraints from the repo
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). So GitHub Actions must still open and complete the `ai-review` check.
- Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:7`).
- The App key has only been used from the desktop runner (`notes/findings.md:4`).
- The routine returns 200 when the review passes, 422 when it has blocking findings, and any other status when it fails. A call can take up to 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
- The NAS runner can make HTTP calls. It cannot run the reviewer CLI (`README.md:23`).
- All reviewers share one sign-in. If two sessions refresh it at the same moment, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:2-3`).

## Steps
1. **Write the eval first.** Add a stub HTTP server and a test for a new script, `scripts/call_routine.sh`. The test must fail before the script exists.
   - **Cases:** 200 → exit 0. 422 → exit 1. 500, 401, connection refused or a hang → exit 2.
   - **Request check:** the stub confirms the request carried the bearer header and the JSON body `{pull_request (a number), model, effort}`.
   - **Wrong twin:** a version that maps 422 to 0 must fail the test. Undoing the script must fail it again.
   - **Hang case:** the time limit can be overridden by an env variable, so the test does not wait 31 minutes.
2. **Write `scripts/call_routine.sh`.**
   - Build the body with `jq` and send it with `curl -w '%{http_code}'`. Do not use `-f`, which hides the status code.
   - Default `--max-time` is about 1860s (31 minutes). Map curl errors to exit 2.
   - Pass the token through a header file, so it does not show in `ps` on the runner.
   - Log the response body, so failures can be diagnosed.
3. **Run a smoke test on the new runner.** Add a `workflow_dispatch` job that does three things:
   - checks that `gh`, `jq` and `curl` are installed
   - mints the App token
   - opens and completes an `ai-review` check on a test SHA that is not the head of any open PR

   This proves the App key works away from the desktop. The job must be on the default branch before it can be dispatched.
4. **Set up the variables.** Create the variable `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` and the secret `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN`. Keep `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`; they now go in the request body.
5. **Switch both workflows.**
   - Change `runs-on` and replace the `start_review.sh` step with `call_routine.sh`.
   - Set `timeout-minutes: 35`.
   - Keep the token mint, `check_run.sh`, the `ai-review` name, and the `if: always()` complete step that uses `job.status`.
   - Do not add `cancel-in-progress`. Cancelling the job stops curl but does not stop the routine, so an old and a new review would overlap.
   - Do not add a global `concurrency` group either. GitHub keeps only one pending run per group and cancels the rest, so reviews would be lost.
   - Result: a 422, a routine failure and a timeout all fail the check, so merge is blocked.
6. **Run live trials.**
   - On the PR that makes the switch: a clean PR turns the check green, and a PR with a planted blocking issue turns it red and blocks merge.
   - Force one routine failure and confirm the check fails.
   - Confirm the App still creates the check.
   - After merge, test `/rereview`. `issue_comment` always runs the workflow from the default branch, so it cannot be tested earlier.
7. **Watch for a lost sign-in.** If the sign-in is lost, every PR is blocked until someone seeds it again.
   - Alert when `call_routine.sh` exits 2.
   - Check that the cloud sign-in still refreshes when no review runs for 10 days.
   - After cutover, stop the desktop reviewer from using the shared sign-in, so only the cloud session refreshes it.
8. **Retire the desktop after a trial period of real PRs.**
   - Remove `scripts/start_review.sh` with `git rm` in the same step, so a rollback commit can bring the workflows and the script back together.
   - Update the README: the intro, the line about `start_review.sh`, the workflow table and the NAS "Use" column.

## Decisions for you
- **Runner: NAS or `ubuntu-latest`.**
  - On the NAS, each review holds the runner for up to 30 minutes. The NAS has one runner, so reviews queue one at a time. That also lowers the chance of a sign-in refresh collision.
  - `ubuntu-latest` already has the tools and runs reviews in parallel. It needs the App key to work from GitHub's machines, and the routine URL must be reachable from there.
- **`/rereview` permissions.** Any commenter can start a review today, and each review now costs money. You could limit it with an `author_association` check.

Fork PRs get no secrets, so their required check stays pending. That is how it works today, and the plan does not change it.

+name: review-smoke

+# ai-review check run. Use a SHA that is not the head of an open pull request,
+# so the green check cannot clear a real pull request.
+on:

+    inputs:
+      head_sha:
+        description: Commit SHA to write a test ai-review check run on
+        required: true
+
+jobs:
+  smoke:
+    runs-on: [self-hosted, nas]
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - name: Check tools
+        run: |
+          for tool in gh jq curl; do
+            command -v "$tool" || { echo "::error::$tool is missing"; exit 1; }
+          done
+      - id: app-token
+        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1
+        with:
+          app-id: ${{ vars.REVIEW_APP_ID }}
+          private-key: ${{ secrets.REVIEW_APP_KEY }}
+      - name: Refuse the head of an open pull request
+        run: |
+          [[ "$HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { echo "::error::head_sha must be a full 40-character SHA"; exit 1; }

+          fi

+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ inputs.head_sha }}

+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ inputs.head_sha }}

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine (docs/cloud-routine.md) and waits for it.
+# Exit 0: review passed (200). Exit 1: blocking findings (422).
+# Exit 2: the routine failed, timed out, or could not be reached.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=${1:-}
+max_time=${CLOUD_ROUTINE_MAX_TIME:-1860}
+
+if ! [[ "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+  echo "::error::usage: call_routine.sh <pull request number>"
+  exit 2
+fi
+for name in CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN REVIEW_MODEL REVIEW_EFFORT; do
+  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
+    echo "::error::$name is not set"
+    exit 2
+  fi
+done
+
+# RUNNER_TEMP is emptied after each job, so the token file does not outlive it.
+work=$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/routine.XXXXXX")
+trap 'rm -r "$work"' EXIT
+# The header goes through a file so the token stays off the process list.
+printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" > "$work/auth"
+
+jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "$REVIEW_MODEL" \
+  --arg effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}' > "$work/body"
+
+curl_exit=0
+status=$(curl -sS -X POST \
+  --max-time "$max_time" \
+  -H @"$work/auth" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data-binary @"$work/body" \
+  -o "$work/response" \
+  -w '%{http_code}' \
+  "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL") || curl_exit=$?
+
+echo "routine response (HTTP ${status:-none}):"
+cat "$work/response" 2>/dev/null || true
+echo
+
+if [ "$curl_exit" -ne 0 ]; then
+  echo "::error::cloud routine call failed (curl exit $curl_exit); the review may still be running in the cloud"
+  exit 2
+fi
+case "$status" in
+  200) exit 0 ;;
+  422) echo "::error::reviewer reported blocking findings"; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "::error::cloud routine failed with HTTP $status; check the reviewer sign-in"; exit 2 ;;
+esac

+Usage: stub_routine.py <mode> <port_file> <record_file>

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks scripts/call_routine.sh against a stub of the cloud routine.
+# Usage: tests/test_call_routine.sh [script]   (default: scripts/call_routine.sh)
+set -uo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+script=${1:-$here/../scripts/call_routine.sh}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+stub_pid=
+trap '[ -n "$stub_pid" ] && kill "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null; rm -r "$work"' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+start_stub() {
+  : > "$work/port"
+  : > "$work/request"
+  python3 "$here/stub_routine.py" "$1" "$work/port" "$work/request" &
+  stub_pid=$!
+  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && return; sleep 0.1; done
+  echo "stub did not start" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+
+stop_stub() {
+  kill "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null
+  wait "$stub_pid" 2>/dev/null
+  stub_pid=
+}
+
+run_script() {
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=$1 CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=test-model REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_MAX_TIME=2 \
+    bash "$script" 42 > "$work/out" 2>&1
+}
+
+expect() {
+  local name=$1 want=$2 got=$3
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
+    echo "PASS $name"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL $name: want exit $want, got $got"
+    sed 's/^/    /' "$work/out"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}
+
+for case in "200 0" "422 1" "500 2" "401 2" "403 2"; do
+  set -- $case
+  start_stub "$1"
+  run_script "http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire"
+  expect "status $1" "$2" "$?"
+  stop_stub
+done
+
+# A hang times out. While the call waits, the token must not be on any
+# process command line.
+start_stub hang
+run_script "http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire" &
+script_pid=$!
+sleep 1
+ps -eo args > "$work/ps"
+wait "$script_pid"
+expect "hang" 2 "$?"
+stop_stub
+if grep -q 'test-token' "$work/ps"; then
+  echo "FAIL token on a process command line"
+  failures=$((failures + 1))
+else
+  echo "PASS token not on a process command line"
+fi
+
+# Missing configuration fails as a routine failure.
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9/fire REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e \
+  bash "$script" 42 > "$work/out" 2>&1
+expect "missing token" 2 "$?"

+  REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=e bash "$script" > "$work/out" 2>&1
+expect "missing pull request number" 2 "$?"
+
+# Connection refused: take a free port, then close it.
+start_stub 200
+port=$(cat "$work/port")
+stop_stub
+run_script "http://127.0.0.1:$port/fire"
+expect "connection refused" 2 "$?"
+
+# The request carries the token and the documented body.
+start_stub 200
+run_script "http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire"
+stop_stub
+if jq -e '.authorization == "Bearer test-token"
+    and .content_type == "application/json"
+    and .body == {"pull_request": 42, "model": "test-model", "effort": "high"}' \
+    "$work/request" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "PASS request shape"
+else
+  echo "FAIL request shape: $(cat "$work/request")"
+  failures=$((failures + 1))
+fi

+if grep -q 'test-token' "$work/out"; then
+  echo "FAIL token printed in output"
+  failures=$((failures + 1))
+else
+  echo "PASS token not printed"
