+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs fire_cloud_routine.sh against a local stub of the cloud routine and checks each status maps to the right exit code.
+set -uo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/stub.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
+        with open(sys.argv[2], "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": body}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+open(sys.argv[1], "w").write(str(server.server_port))
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 -I "$work/stub.py" "$work/port" "$work/request" &
+server=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [[ -s $work/port ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+port=$(cat "$work/port")
+
+export CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret-token REVIEW_MODEL=model-a REVIEW_EFFORT=high
+failures=0
+expect() {
+  local want=$1 status=$2
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/$status" "$here/fire_cloud_routine.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local got=$?
+  if [[ $got == "$want" ]]; then echo "ok   status $status -> exit $got"; else echo "FAIL status $status -> exit $got, want $want"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+expect 0 200
+want_request='{"auth": "Bearer secret-token", "body": {"pull_request": 42, "model": "model-a", "effort": "high"}}'
+if [[ $(cat "$work/request") == "$want_request" ]]; then echo "ok   request body and token"; else echo "FAIL request: $(cat "$work/request")"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+expect 1 422
+expect 1 500
+expect 1 401
+# Nothing listens on port 1, so curl fails to connect.
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1/ "$here/fire_cloud_routine.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+if [[ $? == 1 ]]; then echo "ok   unreachable routine -> exit 1"; else echo "FAIL unreachable routine"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/200" "$here/fire_cloud_routine.sh" '42,"x":1' >/dev/null 2>&1
+if [[ $? == 2 ]]; then echo "ok   bad pull request number -> exit 2"; else echo "FAIL bad pull request number"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi

+import http.server, json, sys
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
+        ok = (self.headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer t0ken"

+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a): pass
+http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
+EOF
+port=18765
+python3 "$work/stub.py" "$port" &
+server=$!
+sleep 1
+
+fail=0
+check() {
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/$1" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t0ken REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$root/scripts/fire_routine.sh" 7 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  got=$?
+  if [ "$got" -eq "$2" ]; then echo "ok   status $1 -> exit $got"; else echo "FAIL status $1 -> exit $got, want $2"; fail=1; fi
+}

+check 422 1
+check 500 1
+check 400 1
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:1/200" CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t0ken REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+  "$root/scripts/fire_routine.sh" 7 >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "FAIL unreachable routine -> exit 0"; fail=1; } || echo "ok   unreachable routine -> exit 1"
+exit $fail

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks that start_review.sh sends the pull request number, model and effort
+# in the JSON body of its POST to the cloud routine. A stub curl records the
+# request instead of sending it.
+set -euo pipefail

+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+

+#!/bin/bash
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --data) printf '%s' "$2" > "$STUB_DIR/body"; shift ;;
+  esac
+  shift
+done
+printf 200
+STUB
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl"
+

+  REVIEW_MODEL=test-model REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.invalid/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token \
+  "$script_dir/start_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null
+
+if [ ! -f "$work/body" ]; then
+  echo "FAIL: start_review.sh sent no JSON body" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+expected='{"effort":"high","model":"test-model","pull_request":42}'
+actual=$(jq -cS . "$work/body")
+if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
+  echo "FAIL: body was $actual, expected $expected" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi

+import http.server, pathlib, sys

+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        (work / "body.json").write_bytes(body)
+        self.send_response(200)

 #!/bin/bash
+# Starts a review on the cloud routine (see docs/cloud-routine.md) and waits for it.
+# Exit 0 when the review passed, 1 on blocking findings, 2 when the routine failed.
 set -euo pipefail
 pull_request_number=$1
-reviewer exec review \
-  --model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
-  --effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
-  --pull-request "$pull_request_number" \
-  --post-comments
+model=${REVIEW_MODEL:?}
+effort=${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}
+if [[ ! $pull_request_number =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+  echo "pull request number must be digits: $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2
+fi
+# Plain tokens only, so the JSON body needs no escaping and no jq on the runner.
+for value in "$model" "$effort"; do
+  if [[ ! $value =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
+    echo "model and effort must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]+: $value" >&2; exit 2
+  fi
+done
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%s,"model":"%s","effort":"%s"}' "$pull_request_number" "$model" "$effort")
+# The routine holds the request open for up to 30 minutes.
+status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/stderr -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1860 \
+  -X POST \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  --data "$body" \
+  "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}") || status=000

+  422) echo "review reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;

meta.prior_reply:
I read all seven files in the repository. A separate verifier agent checked each risk below against the files and confirmed it. The verifier also found the extra items in the second list. I edited no files.

## Main risks

1. **The check run cannot move to the cloud.** The cloud proxy blocks writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:5`). Branch protection needs the `ai-review` check to pass before a merge (`notes/findings.md:7`). So a GitHub-side runner must still open and complete the check, and the cloud routine does only the review. If nothing writes the check, no pull request can merge.

2. **The NAS runner suits short jobs.** The README says the NAS handles "Short jobs and HTTP calls" (`README.md:23`). The routine's POST can block for up to 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). If the NAS has only one runner, reviews will queue behind each other. A GitHub-hosted runner is the other choice.

3. **The App key would run from a new host.** `REVIEW_APP_KEY` has only ever run on the desktop (`notes/findings.md:6`). Moving the token steps puts that key and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` on a host where they have never been. App tokens also last about one hour, which comes from general GitHub knowledge, not the repo. A token minted before a 30-minute wait leaves a thin margin for the complete step.

4. **A blocking review can pass by mistake.** The routine returns 200 for a pass, 422 for blocking findings, and any other status for a failure (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). Both workflows set the check result from `job.status` (`pr-review.yml:27`, `rerun-review.yml:28`). Plain `curl` exits 0 on a 422. Without `--fail` and an explicit status mapping, the check reports success on blocking findings. The trials did not test the 422 path.

5. **The shared reviewer sign-in can fail.** All cloud sessions share one sign-in, seeded once at setup (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`). It refreshes about every 10 days, and two refreshes at the same moment can sign a session out (`notes/findings.md:4`). The trials ran on one day, so a refresh was probably not tested. That is a guess, because the repo gives no setup date. If the sign-in is lost, every review fails until someone seeds it again, and the required check blocks all merges.

6. **The concurrency trial was thin.** It ran two reviews at once and recorded only "exit 0" (`notes/findings.md:3`). It did not record whether the comments posted correctly or what HTTP status the routine returned.

7. **More reviews will overlap.** Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` group. Today the one desktop runner makes jobs wait in line. Cloud sessions run in parallel, so quick pushes start overlapping reviews of the same pull request. That also raises the chance of the concurrent refresh in risk 5.

8. **The check can land on a commit the review did not see.** The routine body carries a pull request number but no head SHA (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The routine reviews whatever head exists when it runs, and the check uses the event's SHA. `rerun-review.yml` also looks up the head SHA twice, once at open and once at complete (`scripts/check_run.sh:10,12`). A push during a long review can split those onto different commits.

9. **Comment posting in the cloud is untested.** The routine posts review comments itself. The proxy finding covers only check runs, so nothing shows that the proxy allows comment writes. Nothing says which identity will post the comments. The current identity is also undocumented: the reviewer step gets no `GH_TOKEN`.

10. **Timeouts can cause duplicate comments.** The HTTP client and any proxy on the runner must allow more than 30 minutes. If the connection drops, the result is unknown and the routine may still post comments. A retry can then post the comments twice.

## Other points the verifier found

- **Anyone can trigger a rerun.** `/rereview` has no check on who commented (`rerun-review.yml:8`). In the cloud, any commenter can start paid runs.
- **Opened check runs stay open.** `complete` creates a new check run and does not update the open one (`scripts/check_run.sh:11-12`). Every review leaves an `in_progress` run behind. This problem exists today.
- **Fork pull requests get no secrets.** This comes from general GitHub knowledge. On the `pull_request` trigger, fork pull requests receive no secrets, so the token step fails for them.
- **Model and effort need wiring.** `vars.REVIEW_MODEL` and `vars.REVIEW_EFFORT` must go into the POST body. Today they reach the reviewer as environment variables.
- **Logs will move to the cloud.** The review logs will be in the cloud session, so the Actions log will no longer show why a review failed.
- **The README will be out of date.** `README.md:5-7` and `README.md:16` describe the desktop flow.

Several rule guides named in `.claude/rules/index.md` are missing from the repository. Only `.claude/docs/rule-guides/verified-work.md` exists.

+set -uo pipefail

+work=$(mktemp -d)

+failures=0

+check() {
+  if [ "$1" = "$2" ]; then echo "ok   $3"; else echo "FAIL $3 (got '$1', want '$2')"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi

+        self.send_response(code)
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *args):

I read every file in the repo and changed nothing. A separate verifier agent checked each claim below against the files and confirmed all 11. It also ran two live tests: `curl` against a local server that returns 422, and `gh api --help`.

## Risks, most serious first

**1. The cloud cannot write the `ai-review` check, and merges depend on it.**
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`), so a GitHub Actions job still has to open and close the check.
- Merges require `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). A check that never closes blocks every merge. A check that passes by mistake lets unreviewed code merge.

**2. A simple port would mark blocking findings as a pass.**
- The routine returns 422 when the reviewer finds blocking issues (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). Plain `curl` exits 0 on a 422; the verifier tested this. The check takes its result from `job.status` (`pr-review.yml:27`), so `ai-review` would pass.
- Adding `--fail` alone makes a blocking finding and a broken routine look the same. The workflow should map 200, 422 and every other status to separate results.

**3. Parallel reviews can sign out the one shared reviewer account.**
- Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` group, so several pushes or `/rereview` comments start several runs at once.
- When two sessions refresh the sign-in at the same moment, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:2`).
- The concurrency trial shows only that both runs exited 0 (`notes/findings.md:1`). It does not show that either review was correct.

**4. Nobody has a plan for a lost sign-in.**
- The sign-in was set up once (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`) and has to refresh about every 10 days. No file says how to restore it after a sign-out.
- During a cutover, desktop and cloud sessions may share the same account and race each other on refresh.

**5. The check can mark the wrong commit as passed.**
- `check_run.sh:11-12` creates a new check run to close out a review. It never updates the run it opened, so every review leaves an old run stuck `in_progress`.
- In `rerun-review.yml`, `open-for-pr` and `complete-for-pr` each look up the PR's latest commit separately. If someone pushes during a review, the pass lands on the new, unreviewed commit. A cloud run can take up to 30 minutes, which widens this window.

**6. The runner that sends the request is untested.**
- The NAS runner is meant for "short jobs and HTTP calls" (`README.md:23`). A request that waits up to 30 minutes is a long job for it.
- Nothing shows that a proxy or client timeout keeps a 30-minute connection open. If the connection drops, the routine may still post comments while the check fails, and a retry posts the review twice.
- The App private key has only been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). Creating the token on another runner has never been tried.

**7. Anyone can start paid runs.** `rerun-review.yml:8` does not check who wrote the `/rereview` comment. Today that only adds load to the desktop. On the cloud, every comment costs money and adds to the sign-in race in risk 3.

**8. Nobody has tested comment posting from the cloud.** The routine posts review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The proxy trial covered only check-runs writes.

**9. The workflows still need wiring.** Neither workflow uses `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` or `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` yet. `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT` would have to move from environment variables into the request body.

One repo note: `.claude/rules/index.md` links to about 15 rule guides, but only `verified-work.md` exists in the repo. I applied the other rules from their one-line summaries.

+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+script=${START_REVIEW:-$repo/scripts/start_review.sh}
+work=$(mktemp -d)

+cat > "$work/server.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+log = sys.argv[1]
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(log, "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers["Authorization"], "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        self.send_response(int(self.path.strip("/")))
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b'{"ok": true}')

+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(log + ".port", "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_port))

I read every file in the repo. A separate verifier agent checked each claim against the files: 10 were confirmed, 1 was corrected (it is fixed below), and 1 is only a note. Only the risks those checks support are listed here. I edited no files.

## Risks of moving PR reviews to the cloud routine

**1. The required check can block every merge.**
- Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). The repo has no settings file to confirm this, so it rests on the note alone.
- The reviewer sign-in in the cloud session was set up once, by hand (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`). It must refresh about every 10 days. Two sessions refreshing at the same moment can sign one out (`notes/findings.md:2`).
- No file says how to restore the sign-in. Once it is signed out, every review fails, and no pull request can merge until someone fixes it by hand.

**2. Parallel reviews share one sign-in.**
- Neither workflow sets a `concurrency` group (`pr-review.yml`, `rerun-review.yml`). Each push and each `/rereview` starts its own run.
- Finding 1 (`notes/findings.md:1`) reports only that two parallel reviews exited 0. Nobody checked the review output or the posted comments, so parallel use is not proven safe.
- More parallel sessions also make the refresh race in risk 1 more likely.

**3. The cloud session cannot write the check run.**
- The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). A GitHub-side runner must still open and complete `ai-review`, so the move is never fully off GitHub runners.

**4. The App private key would be used somewhere new.**
- The key has only ever run on the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). If the NAS or a GitHub-hosted runner now mints the App token, that path has never been tested. Keep the key out of the cloud session.

**5. A 422 can show as a pass.**
- The routine returns `200` for pass, `422` for blocking findings, and any other status for failure (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
- Today the check result comes from `${{ job.status }}` (`pr-review.yml:27`). A plain `curl` exits 0 on a 422, so blocking findings would mark the check as passed.
- The step must read the HTTP status and treat 422 and other failures as different outcomes. Otherwise a routine outage looks the same as a bad review.

**6. The call can wait up to 30 minutes.**
- The POST waits until the review ends, up to 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
- The NAS is meant for "short jobs and HTTP calls" (`README.md:23`). A 30-minute wait is not short.
- A dropped connection, or a curl or proxy timeout, fails the check even if the review finishes. A review that runs past 30 minutes also fails.

**7. Comment posting is untested.**
- The routine posts review comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). No file says which GitHub identity it uses.
- No trial checked whether the proxy allows writes for PR comments. It already blocks check-runs writes.
- Today the reviewer uses login details already stored on the desktop (`start_review.sh:8`; the step gets no `GH_TOKEN`).

**8. A longer review window makes existing check-run bugs worse.**
- `rerun-review` looks up the head SHA once when it opens the check and again when it completes it (`check_run.sh:10,12`). If someone pushes during the review, the pass or fail lands on a commit the reviewer never saw. The old commit keeps a check stuck at `in_progress`.
- Every action creates a new check run with a POST (`check_run.sh:9-12`). Each review leaves a second `in_progress` run that is never closed.

**9. Anyone who can comment can start a paid review.**
- `/rereview` does not check who wrote the comment, and `startsWith` also matches text like `/rereviewxyz` (`rerun-review.yml:8`).
- In the cloud, each match costs a paid review and adds another session to the sign-in race in risks 1 and 2.

**10. The settings must be mapped by hand.**
- The routine takes `model` and `effort` in the JSON body (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). Today they come from `REVIEW_MODEL` and `REVIEW_EFFORT`. No file describes how to map one to the other.

## Limits of this check
- The findings come from yesterday's trial notes. I did not call the routine or query GitHub, because the repo has no remote.
- The rules index links many guides, but only `verified-work.md` is in the repo, so I applied only that one.

The risks most likely to block the move are 1, 3 and 5. Risk 1 can stop all merges, risk 3 means GitHub runners stay part of the setup, and risk 5 can let blocking findings pass.

+"""Stand-in for the cloud routine. The URL path picks the reply: /200, /422, /500, /hang."""
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
+
+log_path = sys.argv[1]
+
+
+class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
+        body = self.rfile.read(length).decode()
+        with open(log_path, "a") as log:
+            log.write(json.dumps({
+                "path": self.path,
+                "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                "body": body,
+            }) + "\n")
+        if self.path == "/hang":
+            time.sleep(5)
+            return
+        status = int(self.path.lstrip("/"))
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b'{"result":"stub"}')
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+print(server.server_port, flush=True)
+server.serve_forever()

I read every file in the repository. A separate verifier agent checked each claim below against the files and confirmed all of them. I changed no files.

## Risks, most severe first

**1. Merges can be blocked, or a check can pass on a commit nobody reviewed**
- Branch protection requires the `ai-review` check to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`).
- The cloud session's proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). So the routine cannot open or complete the check itself.
- An Actions job must still own the check. The only always-on runner is the NAS, which can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer (`README.md:23`).
- If that job does not get to complete the check, every PR stays blocked.

**2. The HTTP status must be mapped to a check result**
- The routine returns 200 for a pass, 422 for blocking findings, and any other code for a routine failure (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
- Today the check result comes only from `job.status` (`pr-review.yml:27`, `rerun-review.yml:28`).
- If the call does not fail the step on a 422, a review with blocking findings passes the check.
- With the current setup, "routine failed" and "blocking findings" both show as `failure`, and the author cannot tell which one happened.

**3. The shared reviewer sign-in can expire or get signed out**
- The sign-in must refresh about every 10 days. Two refreshes at the same moment can sign one session out (`notes/findings.md:4`).
- The cloud sign-in was set up once (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`). Nothing says how it gets refreshed after that.
- Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` group. A push and a `/rereview` comment can start two reviews at once.
- If the desktop and the cloud share one sign-in during the move, they can sign each other out.

**4. Exit 0 does not prove a review happened**
- In the trial, two reviews at the same time on one sign-in both exited 0 (`notes/findings.md:1`). Nothing shows that anyone checked the posted comments.

**5. The review can cover a different commit than the check**
- The routine and `start_review.sh:7` review by PR number. They do not pin a commit.
- `pr-review` attaches the check to the commit that triggered the event. `rerun-review` looks up the head commit twice, once when it opens the check and once when it completes it (`check_run.sh:10,12`).
- A review can take up to 30 minutes. A push during that time can put a pass on a commit that was never reviewed.

**6. Each review leaves a stuck check run behind**
- The "complete" step sends a POST to `/check-runs` (`check_run.sh:11-12`). A POST creates a new check run, so the first run stays `in_progress`.
- The fix is to keep the id from "open" and update that run with a PATCH. The migration should not copy the current pattern.

**7. The 30-minute request can time out or keep running after the job ends**
- The POST blocks for up to 30 minutes. No file sets a client timeout, and nothing confirms that the NAS or a proxy will keep the connection open that long.
- The routine has no cancel endpoint. If the job is cancelled or the runner dies, the routine still posts comments and the check stays open.
- The NAS is meant for short jobs. One blocking call per PR can fill its job queue.

**8. Credentials move to new places**
- The App private key has only been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). If the job moves to the NAS, the key is stored there for the first time.
- `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` becomes a new secret to protect.
- The docs do not say which identity the routine uses to post comments (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The repo does not show which identity posts them today either.

**9. Anyone can trigger `/rereview`**
- `rerun-review.yml:8` does not check who wrote the comment. `startsWith` also matches text such as `/rereviewXYZ`.
- Each trigger costs a review, uses the secrets, and adds load on the shared sign-in (risk 3).

Some risks rest only on yesterday's trial notes (`notes/findings.md`). I had no GitHub, proxy, or routine access, so nothing here was tested live. I edited no files.

## Blocking risks

1. **The routine cannot write the `ai-review` check.** The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). Branch protection requires that check to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). If no other host writes it, every PR is blocked from merging. Another host must call the routine and record the result. The NAS can make HTTP calls but cannot run the reviewer (`README.md:23`), so it is the likely caller.
2. **The App key has never been used outside the desktop.** The review App's private key has only been used from the desktop runner (`notes/findings.md:4`). Creating the token on the NAS or any other runner is untested.
3. **One lost sign-in blocks every PR.** All reviews share one reviewer sign-in, created once at setup (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`). It refreshes about every 10 days. Two sessions refreshing at once can sign one out (`notes/findings.md:2`). Then every review fails, and the required check blocks all merges. The repo has no fallback and no documented way to sign in again.
4. **Overlapping reviews raise that risk.** Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` group. Fast pushes, or a push plus `/rereview`, start overlapping cloud sessions on the one sign-in. Only one concurrent trial was run, and it passed (`notes/findings.md:1`).

## Behaviour changes that need new code

5. **Mapping the result is new logic.** Today the check result is `job.status` (`pr-review.yml:27`), which follows the reviewer's exit code. The routine returns 200 for a pass, 422 for blocking findings, and any other status for a routine failure (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). The caller must map these three cases. A routine failure should not look the same as blocking findings.
6. **The caller waits up to 30 minutes on one request.** The caller's HTTP timeout must be longer than 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). The docs do not say what happens at the limit. A dropped connection can mark the check failed while the routine still posts comments. A retry can then post the comments twice.
7. **The token's time margin is small.** GitHub App installation tokens last about one hour (GitHub's documented behaviour; the repo does not show it). A 30-minute review plus time in the queue fits, but with little spare time.
8. **Comments may come from a different account.** The routine posts comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The docs do not say which account it posts as. Today the reviewer CLI on the desktop posts them (`scripts/start_review.sh:8`).

## Existing defects that the move makes worse

9. **Each review creates two check runs.** The `complete` and `complete-for-pr` steps create a new check run instead of updating the open one (`scripts/check_run.sh:11-12`). If the complete step fails, a run stays `in_progress`.
10. **The review and the check can be on different commits.** The reviewer gets only the PR number (`start_review.sh:7`), and so does the routine (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). `rerun-review.yml` looks up the head commit once at open and again at complete (`check_run.sh:10,12`). If someone pushes during a review, a pass can land on a commit nobody reviewed. Longer cloud reviews make this more likely.
11. **Anyone who can comment can start a review.** `rerun-review.yml:8` has no check on who wrote the comment. That cost and the sign-in risk now land on the cloud routine.
12. **A failed token step hides its real error.** The complete step runs `if: always()`, even with an empty `GH_TOKEN`. Its error then masks the real cause.

## Not settled from the repo

- Whether the `CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL` variable and the `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` secret exist.
- Whether branch protection requires `ai-review` to come from the review App.
- What exit code the reviewer CLI returns for blocking findings.

## Risks that can block merges

1. **The routine cannot write the `ai-review` check.** The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:5`). Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:7`). So a GitHub Actions job still has to open the check, call the routine, and complete the check. That job needs a runner other than the desktop.
2. **The App key will be used from a new place.** The check-runs calls need a token made from the App key. That key has only ever been used from the desktop runner (`notes/findings.md:6`). The likely new runner is the NAS, which can make HTTP calls (`README.md:23`), or a runner GitHub hosts. Either one is the key's first use outside the desktop, and no test has covered it.
3. **The shared sign-in can sign itself out.** The routine holds one reviewer sign-in, set up once (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`). The sign-in refreshes about every 10 days, and two refreshes at the same moment can sign one session out (`notes/findings.md:4`). Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` group, so a quick run of pushes or a `/rereview` during a review starts reviews in parallel. If the sign-in is lost, every review fails, and every merge is blocked until someone signs in again.
4. **The trial did not prove that parallel reviews work.** Finding 1 only says that two reviews "both finished with exit 0" (`notes/findings.md:3`). It does not say that both posted their comments.

## Risks to correctness

5. **Comment posting from the cloud is untested.** The routine "posts the review comments itself" (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The proxy blocks check-runs writes, and no trial tested PR review or comment writes. If those writes are blocked too, the check can pass while no comments appear.
6. **The result mapping must change.** Today the conclusion comes from `job.status` (`pr-review.yml:27`, `rerun-review.yml:28`). The routine reports through HTTP status: 200 means pass, 422 means blocking findings, and any other code means the routine failed (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). The new step has to map these codes. If it does not, a routine failure looks the same as a review that found problems.
7. **Nothing handles the 30-minute wait.** The POST can stay open for up to 30 minutes. No file sets a client timeout or a `timeout-minutes`, and the docs do not say what happens after 30 minutes. A proxy or NAS idle timeout can cut the call first.
8. **The check can land on the wrong commit.** These faults exist today, and the longer cloud round trip makes them more likely:
   - `complete-for-pr` looks up the head SHA a second time (`scripts/check_run.sh:12`). If someone pushes during a review, the check completes on a different commit from the one it opened on.
   - The reviewer works from the PR number (`scripts/start_review.sh:7`), so it reviews whatever the head is at that moment. The check is still filed on the SHA from the event.
   - The `complete` step creates a second check run and leaves the first one stuck at `in_progress` (`check_run.sh:11-12`), because it never updates the run it opened.

## Risks to access and cost

9. **Anyone who can comment can start a review.** `rerun-review` runs for any comment that starts with `/rereview` (this also matches `/rereviewxyz`). It does not check the commenter's permission (`rerun-review.yml:8`). Each run uses the routine, the shared sign-in, and the `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` secret.

## Limits of this review

- The repository has no git remote. The verifier could not check the branch protection settings or the App settings on GitHub, so items 1 and 2 rest on the trial notes.
- `.claude/rules/index.md` links to many rule guides, and only `verified-work.md` exists in the repository.

I suggest fixing items 3, 5 and 6 before the move: add a concurrency group per PR, test a comment write from the cloud session, and map the HTTP codes to check conclusions. Tell me if you want me to start on any of these.

meta.prior_reply:
I found 10 risks in the repository and its notes. A separate verifier agent checked each one against the files and confirmed all of them, with one exception noted at risk 8. I did not edit any file.

## Risks of moving the reviews to the cloud routine

**Merge gate and check run**

1. **The cloud session cannot write the `ai-review` check, and merges need that check.** The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). A GitHub runner must therefore still mint the App token, call the routine, and write the check run. The NAS is the only other runner (`README.md:23`).
2. **The NAS job would hold a runner for up to 30 minutes.** The routine's POST waits until the review finishes, up to 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). The README lists the NAS for "short jobs and HTTP calls" (`README.md:23`). Long reviews can make other NAS jobs wait. A timeout in the HTTP client or proxy can also cut the call short.
3. **A blocking review can still pass the check.** The routine returns `200` for a pass, `422` for blocking findings, and any other status for a routine failure (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). The workflows send `job.status` as the check's conclusion (`pr-review.yml:27`, `rerun-review.yml:28`). Plain `curl` exits 0 on a `422`, so the job succeeds and the check passes. The step must map 200, 422, other statuses, and the timeout to a conclusion on purpose.
4. **The App private key would be used from a new machine for the first time.** It has only been used from the desktop runner (`notes/findings.md:4`). The NAS has never run `actions/create-github-app-token`.

**Reviewer sign-in**

5. **A sign-in refresh can sign one session out.** The shared sign-in refreshes about every 10 days. When two sessions refresh at the same moment, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:2`). Neither workflow sets `concurrency`, so each push or `/rereview` starts another run alongside any that are still going. A sign-out then makes every review fail until someone signs in again by hand, because the sign-in was "seeded at setup" (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`).
6. **The concurrency evidence is thin.** One trial ran yesterday: two reviews started together and both exited 0 (`notes/findings.md:1`). That trial could not have hit a refresh collision, because refreshes come about every 10 days. Exit 0 also does not show that both reviews posted correct comments. The files do not say whether the desktop and the cloud share one sign-in. If they do, running both during the move adds another collision path.

**Wrong commit or duplicate results**

7. **A result can land on a commit that nobody reviewed.** The routine gets only a pull request number, with no commit SHA (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). It reviews whatever the head is when it starts. `pr-review.yml` writes the result to the SHA from the event (lines 17 and 27). `rerun-review.yml` looks up the head again when the review finishes (`check_run.sh:12`), so a push during the review moves the result to the new commit. The same race exists today, but a 30-minute synchronous call makes the window wider. With no concurrency setting, an older run that finishes late can also overwrite a newer result.
8. **Each review leaves a check run stuck at `in_progress`.** `check_run.sh:9-12` creates a new check run for both `open` and `complete`, and no step updates the first one. This problem exists today. The verifier confirmed the script side. It did not confirm GitHub's API behavior this session, or how branch protection treats two runs with the same name.
9. **A cancelled or retried job does not stop the routine.** If GitHub cancels the NAS job, or the connection drops, the cloud review keeps running and posts its comments. A retry then starts a second review with duplicate comments. This is my inference from the routine posting comments itself (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). No trial covered it.

**Access and identity**

10. **The files do not cover who can trigger a review or who posts comments.**
    - Anyone who can comment can run `/rereview`. The workflow checks only the comment prefix, so `/rereviewfoo` also triggers it (`rerun-review.yml:8`). Each run costs routine time and uses the bearer token.
    - The routine "posts the review comments itself" (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). No file says which identity it uses, or whether the cloud proxy allows writing review comments. The findings test only check-runs writes.
    - Pull requests from forks get no secrets, so the token steps fail for them. This is standard GitHub behavior and the repository does not say it.

Most rule guides that `.claude/rules/index.md` links to are missing from the repository. Only `verified-work.md` exists, and I followed it.

The next step before any build is a trial that settles risks 3, 5 and 10: a forced `422`, two overlapping runs, and one comment post from the cloud.

I read every file in the repository: the README, `docs/cloud-routine.md`, `notes/findings.md`, both workflows and both scripts. A separate verifier agent then checked each claim below against those files and confirmed all of them. I changed no files.

## Risks that can block merges or weaken the merge gate

1. **The cloud routine cannot write the `ai-review` check.** The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). Branch protection requires `ai-review` to pass before a merge (`notes/findings.md:5`). So a GitHub Actions job must still open and complete the check. The only other always-on runner is the NAS, which is listed for "short jobs and HTTP calls" (`README.md:23`). The POST to the routine can block for up to 30 minutes (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`).
2. **Blocking findings can pass the check.** Today the check result comes from `job.status` (`pr-review.yml:27`, `rerun-review.yml:28`). The routine reports blocking findings as HTTP `422` (`docs/cloud-routine.md:7`). A plain POST step can still exit 0 on a 422 and mark the check as passed. The new step must turn 200 into success and every other status into failure. I did not test curl's exit code on a 4xx response this session.
3. **A rerun can pass a commit nobody reviewed.** `check_run.sh` looks up the PR's head commit once at open and again at complete (`scripts/check_run.sh:10,12`). The request to the routine has no commit SHA (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). If someone pushes during the 30-minute review, the check passes on the new head commit, which was not reviewed.
4. **The review and the check can be on different commits.** `pr-review.yml` puts the check on the commit from the event (`:17`, `:27`). The routine reviews whatever the head commit is when it starts.
5. **Every run leaves an `ai-review` check stuck at `in_progress`.** The "complete" step creates a second check run and does not update the first one (`scripts/check_run.sh:11-12`). If the complete step fails, nothing finishes the check and the PR cannot merge.

## Risks to the shared reviewer sign-in

6. **A refresh race can sign the routine out.** The sign-in refreshes about every 10 days, and two refreshes at the same moment can sign one session out (`notes/findings.md:2`). The only evidence that parallel reviews are safe is a single trial with two runs (`notes/findings.md:1`). Even then, "exit 0" does not mean the review passed.
7. **More parallel sessions make that race more likely.** Neither workflow sets `concurrency:`. Every push and every `/rereview` starts its own cloud session on the same sign-in, and the reviews can post duplicate comments.
8. **Nobody watches the sign-in.** It was seeded once at setup (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`), and no file explains how to monitor or re-seed it. If it signs out, every review fails and merges stay blocked until someone re-seeds it.

## Security and credential risks

9. **The App key would be used on a new host.** The review App's private key has only ever been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). Creating its token on the NAS or a GitHub-hosted runner would be the first use anywhere else.
10. **Anyone who can comment can start a paid cloud run.** `rerun-review.yml:8` only checks that the comment starts with `/rereview`. It does not check the commenter's permission. Each such comment would spend `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` usage and add another session on the shared sign-in.
11. **Comment posting is untested.** The doc says the routine posts its own comments (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`). The trials did not test whether the proxy allows that, and the doc does not say which GitHub account posts. If posting fails, the check still gets a result but PR authors see no review.

## Operational risks

12. **The 30-minute request has no timeouts.** Neither workflow sets `timeout-minutes`. The doc does not say what the routine returns at the 30-minute limit, or whether a retry is safe. A connection that sits idle for that long on the NAS could be cut.
13. **The evidence is thin.** Every finding comes from one day of trials (`notes/findings.md:1`).

## Not checked this session

These depend on GitHub's behaviour, and I did not confirm them against GitHub's docs:
- App installation tokens last about one hour, which leaves little margin around a 30-minute review.
- PRs from forks get no secrets. That would leave the App key and `CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN` unavailable for them.

One more thing: the project rules index points to many rule guides, but only `.claude/docs/rule-guides/verified-work.md` exists in the repository. I followed that one guide; the others could not be read.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Eval for scripts/start_review.sh against a fake cloud routine.
+# Usage: scripts/test_start_review.sh
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null; find "$work" -delete' EXIT
+
+cat >"$work/server.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, os, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "request.json"), "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"),
+                       "content_type": self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
+                       "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "status")) as f:
+            status = int(f.read())
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"routine says hi")
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+with open(os.path.join(work, "port"), "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_address[1]))
+server.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 "$work/server.py" "$work" &
+server_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+
+failures=0
+check() {
+  local status=$1 want_exit=$2
+  printf '%s' "$status" >"$work/status"
+  rm -f "$work/request.json"
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/review" \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=test-token \
+  REVIEW_MODEL='model "x"' \
+  REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 >"$work/out" 2>&1
+  local got_exit=$?
+  if [ "$got_exit" != "$want_exit" ]; then
+    echo "FAIL status $status: exit $got_exit, want $want_exit"; cat "$work/out"; failures=$((failures + 1)); return
+  fi
+  if ! jq -e '.auth == "Bearer test-token"
+      and .content_type == "application/json"
+      and .body == {"pull_request": 42, "model": "model \"x\"", "effort": "high"}' \
+      "$work/request.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "FAIL status $status: wrong request"; cat "$work/request.json" 2>/dev/null; failures=$((failures + 1)); return
+  fi
+  echo "ok   status $status -> exit $got_exit"
+}
+
+check 200 0
+check 204 1
+check 422 1
+check 500 1
+check 401 1
+
+for workflow in pr-review rerun-review; do
+  if grep -q 'desktop' "$repo/.github/workflows/$workflow.yml"; then
+    echo "FAIL $workflow.yml still targets the desktop runner"; failures=$((failures + 1))
+  else
+    echo "ok   $workflow.yml off the desktop runner"
+  fi
+done

I read every file in the repository. A fresh verifier agent then checked each claim below against the files and confirmed all of them. I made no edits.

## Risks of moving PR reviews to the cloud routine

**1. A routine failure blocks every merge.**
Branch protection requires the `ai-review` check to pass (`notes/findings.md:5`). The check stays open or fails whenever any of these happen:
- the cloud sign-in expires
- the POST times out
- the routine returns an unexpected status

**2. The routine cannot write the check itself.**
The cloud proxy refuses writes to the check-runs API (`notes/findings.md:3`). A GitHub Actions job must still do these steps:
- mint the App token
- open the check
- hold the POST open for up to 30 minutes
- complete the check

The NAS is the likely host, but the README describes it for "short jobs and HTTP calls" (`README.md:23`), and a 30-minute blocking call is not a short job.

**3. The App key would run from a new machine.**
The review App's private key has only ever been used from the desktop (`notes/findings.md:4`). Moving the check-run job to the NAS or a hosted runner puts the key on a machine it has never run on. That move needs its own test, and it changes who can reach the key.

**4. One shared sign-in can fail for every review.**
- The cloud session holds one reviewer sign-in, seeded at setup (`docs/cloud-routine.md:8`).
- The sign-in refreshes about every 10 days. If two sessions refresh at the same moment, one can be signed out (`notes/findings.md:2`).
- The docs give no way to re-seed the sign-in or to be alerted when it fails.
- If the desktop and the cloud share this sign-in while both are running during the move, they can race each other.

**5. More reviews will run at the same time.**
Neither workflow has a `concurrency:` group (`pr-review.yml`, `rerun-review.yml`). A push and a `/rereview` comment can start two reviews of one PR. One desktop runner probably ran them one after another, but the cloud routine will not. Finding 1 shows only that two parallel reviews both exited 0. It does not show that both reviews did complete work.

**6. Unreviewed code can get a passing check.**
- The POST body has no head SHA (`docs/cloud-routine.md:6`), so the routine reviews whatever commit is the head when it starts.
- `complete-for-pr` looks up the head SHA again when it completes (`scripts/check_run.sh:12`).
- A push during a 30-minute review can therefore mark a commit that nobody reviewed as passed, and branch protection then lets it merge.
- A longer cloud run makes this window wider.

**7. The result mapping must be rewritten correctly.**
Today the conclusion comes from `job.status`. The new job must map the routine's responses like this:
- `200` becomes success.
- `422` becomes failure.
- Every other status becomes failure, and so does a client timeout. If any of these is mapped to success, the required gate passes falsely.

The HTTP client timeout must also be longer than 30 minutes.

**8. The current check-run logic is already fragile.**
`check_run.sh` uses POST for both open and complete, so each call creates a new check run. The first `in_progress` run is left behind. The migration should not assume this behaves well.

**9. Any commenter can start a paid cloud run.**
`rerun-review.yml:8` does not check who wrote the comment, and `startsWith` also matches text such as `/rereviewxyz`. After the move, each trigger starts a cloud review that can run for up to 30 minutes.

**10. A retry can post duplicate comments.**
The routine posts its review comments itself. If the workflow retries after a timeout, the PR can get the same comments twice.

**11. The docs will describe the wrong setup.**
`README.md` still says the review runs on the desktop runner.

Risks 1, 2, 4 and 6 are the ones that can block merges or let unreviewed code merge. I suggest you keep the desktop workflow as a fallback until the cloud path has passed those cases. I can draft a mitigation plan when you want edits.

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%d,"model":"%s","effort":"%s"}' \
+  "$pull_request_number" "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}")
+fire_routine() {
+  # The routine holds the request open until the review ends, up to 30 minutes.
+  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1920 -X POST \
+    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    --data "$body" \
+    "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" || true
+}
+status=$(fire_routine)
+if [[ $status == 5?? ]]; then
+  echo "routine returned $status; retrying once" >&2
+  status=$(fire_routine)
+fi
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "review reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "routine failed with status $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks scripts/call_routine.sh against a fake curl that returns scripted
+# HTTP statuses, and checks that both review workflows use the NAS runner.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+script=${CALL_ROUTINE:-$repo/scripts/call_routine.sh}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+mkdir -p "$work/bin"
+cat > "$work/bin/curl" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+n=$(( $(cat "$FAKE_DIR/count" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) + 1 ))
+echo "$n" > "$FAKE_DIR/count"
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$FAKE_DIR/args.$n"
+status=$(sed -n "${n}p" "$FAKE_DIR/statuses")
+printf '%s' "${status:-000}"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl"
+
+failures=0
+run_case() {
+  local name=$1 statuses=$2 want_exit=$3 want_calls=$4
+  local dir="$work/$name"
+  mkdir -p "$dir"
+  tr ' ' '\n' <<< "$statuses" > "$dir/statuses"
+  FAKE_DIR=$dir PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$script" 42 > "$dir/out" 2>&1
+  local got_exit=$? got_calls
+  got_calls=$(cat "$dir/count" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  local got_status=0; [ "$got_exit" -ne 0 ] && got_status=1
+  if [ "$got_status" -eq "$want_exit" ] && [ "$got_calls" -eq "$want_calls" ]; then
+    echo "PASS $name"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL $name: exit $got_exit (want $want_exit), calls $got_calls (want $want_calls)"
+    sed 's/^/  | /' "$dir/out"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}
+
+run_case pass            "200"     0 1
+run_case blocking        "422"     1 1
+run_case retry_then_pass "503 200" 0 2
+run_case retry_then_block "500 422" 1 2
+run_case retry_then_fail "502 504" 1 2
+run_case client_error    "404"     1 1
+run_case unreachable     "000"     1 1
+
+args=$work/pass/args.1
+if grep -qx 'Authorization: Bearer tok' "$args" \
+  && grep -qx 'https://routine.example/fire' "$args" \
+  && grep -qx '{"pull_request":42,"model":"m1","effort":"high"}' "$args"; then
+  echo "PASS request_shape"
+else
+  echo "FAIL request_shape"; sed 's/^/  | /' "$args" 2>/dev/null; failures=$((failures + 1))
+fi
+
+for wf in pr-review rerun-review; do
+  f=$repo/.github/workflows/$wf.yml
+  if grep -q 'runs-on: \[self-hosted, nas\]' "$f" \
+    && grep -q 'scripts/call_routine.sh' "$f" \
+    && ! grep -q 'start_review.sh' "$f" \
+    && grep -q 'scripts/check_run.sh' "$f"; then
+    echo "PASS workflow_$wf"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL workflow_$wf"; failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+done
+
+echo "$failures failure(s)"
+[ "$failures" -eq 0 ]

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+model=${REVIEW_MODEL:?}
+effort=${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}
+case "$model$effort" in
+  *[\"\\]*) echo "REVIEW_MODEL and REVIEW_EFFORT must not contain quotes or backslashes" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+esac
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%d,"model":"%s","effort":"%s"}' "$pull_request_number" "$model" "$effort")
+response=$(mktemp)
+trap 'rm -f "$response"' EXIT
+
+# The routine holds the request open until the review ends, up to 30 minutes.
+# The token goes in on stdin so it stays out of the process list.
+post() {
+  printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" |
+  curl --silent --show-error --max-time "${ROUTINE_MAX_TIME:-1860}" \
+    --header @- \
+    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    --data "$body" \
+    --output "$response" \
+    --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+    "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" || true
+}
+
+status=$(post)
+cat "$response" >&2
+if [[ $status == 5?? ]]; then
+  echo "routine returned $status; retrying once" >&2
+  status=$(post)
+  cat "$response" >&2
+fi
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "reviewer reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "routine failed with status $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/call_routine.sh against a local mock routine.
+# Each case gives the status codes the mock returns in order, the exit code
+# the script must return, and the number of requests the mock must receive.
+set -uo pipefail
+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat >"$work/mock.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, sys
+state_dir = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(f"{state_dir}/statuses") as f:
+            statuses = f.read().split()
+        with open(f"{state_dir}/count") as f:
+            n = int(f.read() or 0)
+        with open(f"{state_dir}/count", "w") as f:
+            f.write(str(n + 1))
+        with open(f"{state_dir}/last", "w") as f:
+            json.dump({"auth": self.headers["Authorization"], "body": json.loads(body)}, f)
+        code = int(statuses[min(n, len(statuses) - 1)])
+        self.send_response(code)
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"mock")
+    def log_message(self, *a):
+        pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+print(s.server_port, flush=True)
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 -u "$work/mock.py" "$work" >"$work/port" &
+server=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [[ -s $work/port ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+port=$(cat "$work/port")

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud routine for one pull request and waits for the review.
+# Exits 0 when the review passed. Retries once when the routine returns 5xx.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+[[ $pull_request_number =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "bad pull request number: $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+json_string() {
+  local s=${1//\\/\\\\}
+  s=${s//\"/\\\"}
+  printf '"%s"' "$s"
+}
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%s,"model":%s,"effort":%s}' \
+  "$pull_request_number" "$(json_string "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}")" "$(json_string "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}")")
+
+fire() {
+  # The routine holds the POST open until the review finishes, up to 30 minutes.
+  curl -sS --max-time 1860 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
+    -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+    -H @- \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d "$body" <<<"Authorization: Bearer $CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" || true
+}
+
+: "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}"
+# The token goes in on stdin so it stays out of the process list.
+status=$(fire)
+if [[ $status == 5?? ]]; then
+  echo "cloud routine returned $status; retrying once" >&2
+  status=$(fire)
+fi
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "reviewer reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "cloud routine failed with status $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks scripts/run_cloud_review.sh against a stub curl.
+# Each case lists the HTTP statuses the stub returns, the expected exit
+# status of the script, and the expected number of POSTs.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+script=${SCRIPT_UNDER_TEST:-$repo/scripts/run_cloud_review.sh}
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -r -- "$work"' EXIT
+
+mkdir "$work/bin"
+cat >"$work/bin/curl" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+echo "$*" >>"$STUB_DIR/calls"
+[[ " $* " == *" -H @- "* ]] && cat >>"$STUB_DIR/stdin"
+code=$(head -n1 "$STUB_DIR/codes")
+sed -i 1d "$STUB_DIR/codes"
+printf '%s' "$code"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl"
+
+failures=0
+run_case() {
+  local name=$1 codes=$2 want_exit=$3 want_calls=$4
+  local dir="$work/$name"
+  mkdir "$dir"
+  tr ' ' '\n' <<<"$codes" >"$dir/codes"
+  : >"$dir/calls"
+  STUB_DIR=$dir PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret \
+    REVIEW_MODEL='model "x"' REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    bash "$script" 42 >"$dir/out" 2>&1
+  local got_exit=$? got_calls
+  got_calls=$(wc -l <"$dir/calls")
+  if [[ $got_exit -ne $want_exit || $got_calls -ne $want_calls ]]; then
+    echo "FAIL $name: exit $got_exit (want $want_exit), calls $got_calls (want $want_calls)"
+    sed 's/^/    /' "$dir/out"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  else
+    echo "ok   $name"
+  fi
+}
+
+run_case pass            "200"     0 1
+run_case blocking        "422"     1 1
+run_case client-error    "400"     1 1
+run_case no-connection   "000"     1 1
+run_case 5xx-then-pass   "503 200" 0 2
+run_case 5xx-then-block  "502 422" 1 2
+run_case 5xx-twice       "500 504" 1 2
+
+# The body carries the pull request, model and effort as valid JSON, and the
+# bearer token goes in the Authorization header on stdin, never in argv.
+calls="$work/pass/calls"
+stdin="$work/pass/stdin"
+if grep -qF -- '"pull_request":42' "$calls" \
+  && grep -qF -- '"model":"model \"x\""' "$calls" \
+  && grep -qF -- '"effort":"high"' "$calls" \
+  && grep -qF -- '-H @- ' "$calls" \
+  && grep -qF -- 'Authorization: Bearer secret' "$stdin" \
+  && ! grep -qF -- 'secret' "$calls" \
+  && grep -qF -- 'https://routine.example/fire' "$calls"; then
+  echo "ok   request-shape"
+else
+  echo "FAIL request-shape"; sed 's/^/    /' "$calls"
+  failures=$((failures + 1))
+fi
+
+[[ $failures -eq 0 ]] && echo "all passed" || { echo "$failures failed"; exit 1; }

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/call_routine.sh against a local mock routine.
+# Each case gives the statuses the mock returns, in order, then the expected
+# exit code and the expected number of POSTs.
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -r "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/mock.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, os, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "requests"), "a") as f:
+            f.write(json.dumps({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": json.loads(body)}, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "statuses")) as f:
+            statuses = f.read().split()
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "requests")) as f:
+            n = sum(1 for _ in f)
+        self.send_response(int(statuses[min(n, len(statuses)) - 1]))
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a):
+        pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+open(os.path.join(work, "port"), "w").write(str(s.server_port))

+export REVIEW_EFFORT=high
+

+check() {
+  local statuses=$1 want_exit=$2 want_posts=$3
+  echo "$statuses" > "$work/statuses"
+  : > "$work/requests"
+  local got_exit=0

+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi

+check "404"         1 1

+check "503 422"     1 2
+check "502 502 200" 1 2
+check "500 404"     1 2

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine (docs/cloud-routine.md) and waits for the result.
+# Exits 0 when the review passed. Retries once when the routine returns a 5xx status.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+: "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}"
+body=$(jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+
+for attempt in 1 2; do
+  status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1860 \
+    -X POST \
+    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    --data "$body" \
+    "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}") || status=000
+  case "$status" in
+    5??) echo "routine returned $status on attempt $attempt" >&2 ;;
+    *) break ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) echo "review passed" ;;
+  422) echo "reviewer reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  *) echo "routine failed with status $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/call_routine.sh against a local mock routine.
+# Each case gives the statuses the mock returns in order, the expected exit
+# code, and the expected number of POSTs.
+set -uo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'kill "$server_pid" 2>/dev/null; rm -r "$work"' EXIT
+
+cat > "$work/mock.py" <<'EOF'
+import http.server, json, os, sys
+work = sys.argv[1]
+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "requests"), "a") as f:
+            f.write(json.dumps({"auth": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": json.loads(body)}) + "\n")
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "statuses")) as f:
+            statuses = f.read().split()
+        status = int(statuses.pop(0)) if statuses else 500
+        with open(os.path.join(work, "statuses"), "w") as f:
+            f.write(" ".join(statuses))
+        self.send_response(status)
+        self.end_headers()
+    def log_message(self, *a):
+        pass
+s = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+open(os.path.join(work, "port"), "w").write(str(s.server_port))
+s.serve_forever()
+EOF
+python3 "$work/mock.py" "$work" &
+server_pid=$!
+for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$work/port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
+
+failures=0
+run_case() {
+  local statuses=$1 want_exit=$2 want_posts=$3
+  echo "$statuses" > "$work/statuses"
+  : > "$work/requests"
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire" \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$root/scripts/call_routine.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local got_exit=$? got_posts
+  got_posts=$(wc -l < "$work/requests")
+  if [ "$got_exit" = "$want_exit" ] && [ "$got_posts" = "$want_posts" ]; then
+    echo "PASS [$statuses] exit=$got_exit posts=$got_posts"
+  else
+    echo "FAIL [$statuses] exit=$got_exit (want $want_exit) posts=$got_posts (want $want_posts)"
+    failures=$((failures + 1))
+  fi
+}
+
+run_case "200"         0 1
+run_case "422"         1 1
+run_case "400"         1 1
+run_case "500 200"     0 2
+run_case "503 422"     1 2
+run_case "502 504"     1 2
+run_case "500 500 200" 1 2
+run_case "404 200"     1 1
+
+# The request carries the bearer token and the documented body.
+echo "200" > "$work/statuses"
+: > "$work/requests"
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$work/port")/fire" \
+CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=secret REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+  "$root/scripts/call_routine.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+want='{"auth":"Bearer secret","body":{"pull_request":42,"model":"m1","effort":"high"}}'
+got=$(jq -cS . "$work/requests")
+if [ "$got" = "$(echo "$want" | jq -cS .)" ]; then
+  echo "PASS request shape"
+else
+  echo "FAIL request shape: $got"
+  failures=$((failures + 1))
+fi
+
+echo "failures: $failures"
+[ "$failures" = 0 ]

 #!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine (docs/cloud-routine.md) and waits for its verdict.
+# 200 = review passed, 422 = blocking findings, 5xx = retried once, anything else fails.
 set -euo pipefail
 pull_request_number=$1
-reviewer exec review \
-  --model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
-  --effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
-  --pull-request "$pull_request_number" \
-  --post-comments
+[[ "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "pull request number must be numeric" >&2; exit 2; }
+body=$(jq -cn \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+
+fire_routine() {
+  # The routine holds the request open for up to 30 minutes.
+  # The token goes in on stdin so it never shows in the process list.
+  printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" |
+    curl --header @- --silent --show-error --max-time 1860 \
+      --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+      --request POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+      --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+      --data "$body"
+}
+
+for attempt in 1 2; do
+  status=$(fire_routine) || { echo "routine call failed before a response (attempt $attempt)" >&2; exit 1; }
+  case "$status" in
+    200) echo "review passed"; exit 0 ;;
+    422) echo "review reported blocking findings" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+    5??) echo "routine returned $status (attempt $attempt)" >&2 ;;
+    *) echo "routine returned unexpected status $status" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  esac
+done
+echo "routine still failing after one retry" >&2
+exit 1

+#!/bin/bash
+# Checks scripts/start_review.sh against a stub curl that returns scripted statuses.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+mkdir "$work/bin"
+cat > "$work/bin/curl" <<'STUB'
+#!/bin/bash
+# Pops the next status from $STUB_DIR/statuses; "err" simulates a transport failure.
+{ echo "CALL $*"; cat; } >> "$STUB_DIR/calls"
+read -r status rest < "$STUB_DIR/statuses"
+echo "$rest" > "$STUB_DIR/statuses"
+[ "$status" = err ] && exit 7
+printf '%s' "$status"
+STUB
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl"
+
+fails=0
+# run_case <name> <expected exit: 0 or nonzero> <expected calls> <statuses...>
+run_case() {
+  local name=$1 want_exit=$2 want_calls=$3
+  shift 3
+  : > "$work/calls"
+  echo "$*" > "$work/statuses"
+  PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" STUB_DIR="$work" \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+    "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+  local got_exit=$? got_calls
+  got_calls=$(grep -c '^CALL ' "$work/calls")
+  local ok=1
+  if [ "$want_exit" = 0 ]; then [ "$got_exit" = 0 ] || ok=0; else [ "$got_exit" != 0 ] || ok=0; fi
+  [ "$got_calls" = "$want_calls" ] || ok=0
+  if [ "$ok" = 1 ]; then echo "PASS $name"; else echo "FAIL $name (exit=$got_exit calls=$got_calls)"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
+}
+
+run_case "200 passes"                  0 1 200
+run_case "422 fails, no retry"         1 1 422
+run_case "500 then 200 passes"         0 2 500 200
+run_case "503 then 422 fails"          1 2 503 422
+run_case "502 twice fails, one retry"  1 2 502 502
+run_case "404 fails, no retry"         1 1 404
+run_case "transport error, no retry"   1 1 err
+
+# The request carries the bearer token (on stdin, not argv) and the contract's JSON body.
+: > "$work/calls"; echo 200 > "$work/statuses"
+PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" STUB_DIR="$work" \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/fire CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=t \
+  REVIEW_MODEL=m REVIEW_EFFORT=high "$repo/scripts/start_review.sh" 42 > /dev/null 2>&1
+if grep -qx 'Authorization: Bearer t' "$work/calls" \
+  && ! grep '^CALL ' "$work/calls" | grep -q 'Bearer' \
+  && grep -q -- '--max-time 18[0-9][0-9]' "$work/calls" \
+  && grep -qF '{"pull_request":42,"model":"m","effort":"high"}' "$work/calls" \
+  && grep -q 'https://routine.example/fire' "$work/calls"; then
+  echo "PASS request shape"
+else
+  echo "FAIL request shape"; fails=$((fails + 1))
+fi
+
+[ "$fails" = 0 ] && echo "all passed" || { echo "$fails failed"; exit 1; }

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine (docs/cloud-routine.md) and writes the
+# result to $GITHUB_OUTPUT as `result=passed|blocked|failed` and `http_status`.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+body=$(printf '{"pull_request":%d,"model":"%s","effort":"%s"}' \
+  "$pull_request_number" "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}")
+# The routine holds the request open until the review ends, up to 30 minutes.
+http_status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1920 \
+  -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data "$body") || http_status=000
+case "$http_status" in
+  200) result=passed ;;
+  422) result=blocked ;;
+  *) result=failed ;;
+esac
+echo "http_status=$http_status" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?}"
+echo "result=$result" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+echo "Cloud routine returned HTTP $http_status: review $result"
+[ "$result" = passed ]

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine for one pull request and posts the result as a comment.
+# The routine posts the review comments itself; this script reports only the verdict.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+[[ "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "bad pull request number: $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+: "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}"
+
+head_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/pulls/$pull_request_number" -q .head.sha)
+run_url="$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
+body=$(jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" \
+  --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+
+# The routine answers when the review ends, after at most 30 minutes.
+status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1860 \
+  -X POST "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" \
+  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data "$body") || status=000
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) result=pass;    message="✅ **ai-review passed** for $head_sha." ;;
+  422) result=blocked; message="❌ **ai-review found blocking issues** in $head_sha. See the review comments." ;;
+  *)   result=error;   message="⚠️ **ai-review failed to run** for $head_sha (routine returned HTTP $status). Comment \`/rereview\` to try again." ;;
+esac
+
+gh pr comment "$pull_request_number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --body "$message
+
+<sub>ai-review result: \`$result\` · [workflow run]($run_url)</sub>"
+
+[ "$result" = pass ]

+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine for one pull request and comments the result.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+missing=""
+for name in REVIEW_MODEL REVIEW_EFFORT CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN; do
+  [ -n "${!name:-}" ] || missing="$missing $name"
+done
+if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
+  status=none
+  detail="no request was sent, because these values are empty:$missing"
+else
+  body=$(jq -cn \
+    --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+    --arg model "$REVIEW_MODEL" \
+    --arg effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT" \
+    '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+  # The routine holds the request open until the review ends, up to 30 minutes.
+  status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1860 -X POST \
+    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" \
+    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    --data "$body" \
+    "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL") || status=000
+fi
+case "$status" in
+  200) passed=true; message="**AI review: passed.**" ;;
+  422) passed=false; message="**AI review: blocking findings.** Read the review comments on this pull request." ;;
+  *) passed=false; message="**AI review: error.** Reason: ${detail:-the cloud routine returned HTTP $status}. No review result is available." ;;
+esac
+run_url="$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
+gh pr comment "$pull_request_number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
+  --body "$message ([workflow run]($run_url))"
+[ "$passed" = true ]

+#!/bin/bash
+# Runs scripts/cloud_review.sh against stub curl and gh for each routine status.
+set -uo pipefail
+repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -r "$work"' EXIT
+mkdir "$work/bin"
+cat > "$work/bin/curl" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_DIR/curl_args"
+[ "$STUB_STATUS" = 000 ] && { printf 000; exit 28; }
+printf '%s' "$STUB_STATUS"
+EOF
+cat > "$work/bin/gh" <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_DIR/gh_args"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$work/bin/curl" "$work/bin/gh"
+
+failures=0
+check() { # status expected_exit expected_text
+  rm -f "$work/curl_args" "$work/gh_args"
+  STUB_DIR=$work STUB_STATUS=$1 PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" \
+    REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/run \
+    CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN=tok GITHUB_REPOSITORY=o/r GITHUB_SERVER_URL=https://github.com GITHUB_RUN_ID=9 \
+    "$repo/scripts/cloud_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+  local code=$?
+  local result=ok
+  [ "$code" = "$2" ] || result="exit $code, want $2"
+  grep -qF -- "$3" "$work/gh_args" 2>/dev/null || result="$result; comment lacks '$3'"
+  grep -qxF '{"pull_request":42,"model":"m1","effort":"high"}' "$work/curl_args" 2>/dev/null \
+    || result="$result; bad request body"
+  grep -qx 'Authorization: Bearer tok' "$work/curl_args" 2>/dev/null || result="$result; no bearer token"
+  if [ "$result" = ok ]; then echo "PASS status $1"; else echo "FAIL status $1: $result"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
+}
+check 200 0 'AI review: passed.'
+check 422 1 'AI review: blocking findings.'
+check 500 1 'cloud routine returned HTTP 500'
+check 000 1 'cloud routine returned HTTP 000'
+# An empty secret, as on a fork pull request, still produces an error comment.
+rm -f "$work/gh_args"
+STUB_DIR=$work STUB_STATUS=200 PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" REVIEW_MODEL=m1 REVIEW_EFFORT=high \
+  CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL=https://routine.example/run CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN= GITHUB_REPOSITORY=o/r \
+  GITHUB_SERVER_URL=https://github.com GITHUB_RUN_ID=9 "$repo/scripts/cloud_review.sh" 42 >/dev/null 2>&1
+code=$?
+if [ "$code" = 1 ] && grep -qF 'values are empty: CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN' "$work/gh_args" 2>/dev/null; then
+  echo "PASS empty secret"
+else
+  echo "FAIL empty secret: exit $code"; failures=$((failures + 1))
+fi
+exit "$failures"

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+[[ "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "bad pull request number $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2; }
+body=$(jq -n --argjson pr "$pull_request_number" --arg model "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" --arg effort "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}" \
+  '{pull_request: $pr, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+# The routine waits up to 30 minutes for the review to finish.
+status=$(printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
+  --max-time 1860 -X POST -H @- -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body" "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}") || status=000
+case "$status" in
+  200) result="passed"; code=0 ;;
+  422) result="found blocking findings"; code=1 ;;
+  *) result="failed (routine returned HTTP $status)"; code=1 ;;
+esac
+run_url="$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
+gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$pull_request_number/comments" \
+  -f body="**AI review:** the review $result. [Workflow run]($run_url)"
+exit "$code"

@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# Fires the cloud review routine for one pull request and posts the result as a PR comment.
+set -euo pipefail
+pull_request_number=$1
+[[ "$pull_request_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "bad pull request number $pull_request_number" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+umask 077
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+# Headers go through files so the tokens stay out of the process list.
+printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\nContent-Type: application/json\n' "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN:?}" > "$work/routine.headers"
+printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\nAccept: application/vnd.github+json\n' "${GH_TOKEN:?}" > "$work/github.headers"
+
+payload=$(printf '{"pull_request":%s,"model":"%s","effort":"%s"}' \
+  "$pull_request_number" "${REVIEW_MODEL:?}" "${REVIEW_EFFORT:?}")
+
+# The routine holds the request open until the review finishes, up to 30 minutes.
+curl_exit=0
+status=$(curl --silent --show-error --max-time 1860 \
+  --output "$work/response" --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+  -X POST -H "@$work/routine.headers" \
+  --data "$payload" \
+  "${CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL:?}") || curl_exit=$?
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) message='AI review passed.'; exit_code=0 ;;
+  422) message='AI review failed: the reviewer reported blocking findings. See its review comments.'; exit_code=1 ;;
+  *) message="AI review did not complete: the cloud routine returned HTTP ${status:-000} (curl exit $curl_exit)."; exit_code=1 ;;
+esac
+echo "$message"
+
+run_url="$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
+printf '{"body":"%s\\n\\n[Workflow run](%s)"}' "$message" "$run_url" |
+  curl --silent --show-error --fail --max-time 60 --output /dev/null \
+    -X POST -H "@$work/github.headers" \
+    --data @- \
+    "$GITHUB_API_URL/repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$pull_request_number/comments" ||
+  { echo "::error::Could not post the result comment." >&2; exit_code=1; }
+
+exit "$exit_code"

+for name in CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN REVIEW_MODEL REVIEW_EFFORT; do
+  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
+    comment failed "AI review failed to run ($name is not set)."
+    exit 1
+  fi
+done
+
+body=$(jq -n \
+  --argjson pull_request "$pull_request_number" \
+  --arg model "$REVIEW_MODEL" \
+  --arg effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT" \
+  '{pull_request: $pull_request, model: $model, effort: $effort}')
+
+# The routine has one reviewer sign-in, so run one review at a time on this host.
+exec 9>/tmp/cloud-review.lock
+if ! flock --wait 8400 9; then
+  comment failed "AI review timed out waiting for other reviews to finish."
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+# The routine answers when the review finishes, up to 30 minutes.
+routine_max_seconds=${ROUTINE_MAX_SECONDS:-1800}
+started=$SECONDS
+status=$(curl --silent --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' \
+  --max-time 1860 \
+  --request POST \
+  --header "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUD_ROUTINE_TOKEN" \
+  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+  --data "$body" \
+  "$CLOUD_ROUTINE_URL") || status=000
+
+case "$status" in
+  200) comment passed "AI review passed." ;;
+  422) comment blocked "AI review found blocking issues. See the review comments."; exit 1 ;;
+  000)
+    comment failed "AI review failed: no answer from the routine (network error or timeout)." || true
+    # The review can still be running in the cloud. Keep the lock until it must have ended.
+    remaining=$((routine_max_seconds - (SECONDS - started)))
+    if [ "$remaining" -gt 0 ]; then sleep "$remaining"; fi
+    exit 1 ;;
+  *)   comment failed "AI review failed to run (routine returned HTTP $status)."; exit 1 ;;
+esac
